title.zh: 卷十六 列傳第四: 道武七王 明元六王 太武五王
title.en: Volume 16 Biographies 4: Daowu's Seven Sons, Mingyuan's Six Sons, Taiwu's Five Sons
title.raw: 卷十六 列傳第四: 道武七王 明元六王 太武五王 Volume 16 Biographies 4: Daowu's Seven Sons, Mingyuan's Six Sons, Taiwu's Five Sons

sentences.zh: 道武七王 明元六王 太武五王

translations.literal: Seven Sons of Daowu, Six Sons of Mingyuan, Five Sons of Taiwu
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Sons of Daowu, the Six Sons of Mingyuan, and the Five Sons of Taiwu

sentences.zh: 列傳第四道武七王明元六王太武五王

translations.literal: Biographies 4: Seven Sons of Daowu, Six Sons of Mingyuan, Five Sons of Taiwu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 4 — The Seven Sons of Daowu, the Six Sons of Mingyuan, and the Five Sons of Taiwu

sentences.zh: 道武皇帝十男：宣穆劉後生明元皇帝；

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu had ten sons: the Xuanmu Empress Liu bore Emperor Mingyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu had ten sons. Empress Liu the Xuanmu bore Emperor Mingyuan;

sentences.zh: 賀夫人生清河王紹；

translations.literal: Consort He bore Prince of Qinghe Shao;
translations.idiomatic: Consort He bore the Prince of Qinghe, Shao;

sentences.zh: 大王夫人生陽平王熙；

translations.literal: the Great Consort Wang bore Prince of Yangping Xi;
translations.idiomatic: the Great Consort Wang bore the Prince of Yangping, Xi;

sentences.zh: 王夫人生河南王曜；

translations.literal: Consort Wang bore Prince of Henan Yao;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang bore the Prince of Henan, Yao;

sentences.zh: 河間王修、長樂王處文二王母氏闕；

translations.literal: the mothers of Prince of Hejian Xiu and Prince of Changle Chuwén are unknown;
translations.idiomatic: the mothers of the Prince of Hejian, Xiu, and the Prince of Changle, Chuwén, are unrecorded;

sentences.zh: 段夫人生廣平王連、京兆王黎；

translations.literal: Consort Duan bore Prince of Guangping Lian and Prince of Jingzhao Li;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Duan bore the Prince of Guangping, Lian, and the Prince of Jingzhao, Li;

sentences.zh: 皇子渾及聰母氏並闕，皆早薨，無傳。

translations.literal: the princes Hun and Cong—their mothers also unknown—all died young and have no biographies.
translations.idiomatic: the princes Hun and Cong—whose mothers are likewise unknown—all died in childhood and have no biographies.

sentences.zh: 清河王紹字受洛拔，天興六年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Shao, styled Shouluoba, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe, Shao, styled Shouluoba, received his fief in the sixth year of Tianxing.

sentences.zh: 性凶狠險悖，好劫剝行人，斫射犬豕，以為戲樂。

translations.literal: By nature fierce, cruel, and perverse, he delighted in robbing travelers and shooting dogs and pigs for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, cruel, and perverse by nature, he delighted in robbing wayfarers and shooting dogs and pigs for sport.

sentences.zh: 有孕婦，紹剖觀其胎。

translations.literal: When a pregnant woman came along, Shao cut her open to look at the fetus.
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered a pregnant woman, Shao cut her open to inspect the fetus.

sentences.zh: 道武嘗怒之，倒懸井中，垂死乃出。

translations.literal: Daowu once grew angry with him and hung him upside down in a well, pulling him out only when he was near death.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu once flew into a rage and hung him head-down in a well, hauling him out only when he was nearly dead.

sentences.zh: 明元常以義方責之，由此不協。

translations.literal: Mingyuan often rebuked him with moral lessons, and from this they were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan often lectured him on right conduct, and from this the two fell out.

sentences.zh: 而紹母賀夫人有譴，帝將殺之。

translations.literal: Then Shao's mother Lady He was under censure, and the emperor was about to execute her.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shao's mother, Lady He, had been condemned, and the emperor was about to put her to death.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，未決。

translations.literal: Night fell before the decision was made.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell before a decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 賀氏密告急於紹，紹乃與帳下及宦者數人逾宮犯禁。

translations.literal: Lady He secretly sent word of urgency to Shao; Shao then, with men of his retinue and several eunuchs, crossed the palace bounds in violation of the ban.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He secretly sent Shao word of her peril; Shao then crossed the palace bounds with men of his retinue and several eunuchs in defiance of the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 帝驚起，求弓刀不及，暴崩。

translations.literal: The emperor started up in alarm, could not reach bow or blade in time, and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started up in alarm but could not reach bow or blade in time, and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 明日，宮門至日中不開，紹稱詔召百寮於西宮端門前北面，紹從門扇間謂曰：「我有父，亦有兄，公卿欲從誰也？

translations.literal: The next day the palace gates did not open until noon; Shao claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to face north before the western palace's Duan Gate, and from between the door panels said: "I have a father, and I also have an elder brother—which of us do you gentlemen wish to follow?
translations.idiomatic: The next day the palace gates stayed shut until noon. Shao claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to face north before the western palace's Duan Gate, and called from between the door panels: "I have a father, and I have an elder brother—which of us do you gentlemen mean to follow?

sentences.zh: 」王公以下皆失色，莫有對者。

translations.literal: " Princes and officials below all turned pale, and none answered.
translations.idiomatic: " Princes and officials alike turned pale; no one answered.

sentences.zh: 良久，南平公長孫嵩曰：「臣等不審登遐狀。

translations.literal: After a long while Duke of Nanping Changsun Song said: "Your servants do not know the circumstances of Your Majesty's passing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence Duke of Nanping Changsun Song said: "We do not yet know the circumstances of Your Majesty's passing.

sentences.zh: 」唯陰平西元烈哭泣而去。

translations.literal: " Only Yinping Xiyuan Lie wept and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Only Yinping Xiyuan Lie wept and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是朝野凶凶，人懷異志。

translations.literal: Then court and countryside seethed, and every man harbored a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside seethed; every man nursed his own design.

sentences.zh: 肥如侯賀護舉烽於安陽城北，故賀蘭部人皆往赴之。

translations.literal: Marquis of Feiru He Hu raised beacon fires north of Anyang city, and all the old Helan clansmen went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Feiru He Hu raised beacon fires north of Anyang, and all the old Helan clansmen rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 其餘舊部，亦率子弟，招集故人，往往相聚。

translations.literal: The rest of the former followers likewise led sons and younger kin, summoned old comrades, and gathered here and there.
translations.idiomatic: Other former followers likewise led sons and younger kin, called up old comrades, and gathered in bands across the land.

sentences.zh: 紹聞人情不安，乃出布帛班賜王公以下。

translations.literal: Hearing that hearts were unsettled, Shao issued cloth and silk in largesse to princes and officials below.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that hearts were unsettled, Shao distributed cloth and silk in largesse among princes and officials.

sentences.zh: 先是，明元在外，聞變乃還，潛於山中，使人夜告北新侯安同，眾皆回應。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mingyuan had been away; hearing of the upheaval he returned and hid in the mountains, sending men by night to inform Marquis of Beixin An Tong—and the masses answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mingyuan had been away from court. Hearing of the upheaval he returned and hid in the hills, sending men by night to inform Marquis of Beixin An Tong; the masses rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 衛士執送紹，於是賜紹母子死，誅帳下閹官、宮人為內應者十數人。

translations.literal: Guards seized Shao and delivered him up; Shao and his mother were then granted death, and a dozen eunuchs and palace women who had served as inside accomplices were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Guards seized Shao and delivered him up. Shao and his mother were granted death, and a dozen eunuchs and palace women who had served as inside accomplices were put to death.

sentences.zh: 其先犯乘輿者，群臣于城南都街生臠食之。

translations.literal: Those who had first assaulted the imperial carriage were dismembered alive by the ministers at the capital's southern street and eaten.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had first assaulted the imperial carriage were dismembered alive at the capital's southern street and devoured by the ministers.

sentences.zh: 紹時年十六。

translations.literal: Shao was then sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was sixteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 紹母即獻明皇后妹也，美而豔。

translations.literal: Shao's mother was a younger sister of Empress Xianming—beautiful and alluring.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's mother was a younger sister of Empress Xianming, beautiful and alluring.

sentences.zh: 道武如賀蘭部，見而悅之，告獻明後請納焉。

translations.literal: When Daowu visited the Helan tribe he saw her and was pleased; he told Empress Xianming and asked to take her.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu visited the Helan tribe he saw her and was smitten; he told Empress Xianming and asked to take her.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「不可。

translations.literal: The empress said: "You must not.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "You must not.

sentences.zh: 此過美，不善，且已有夫。

translations.literal: She is too beautiful—ill fortune—and she already has a husband.
translations.idiomatic: She is too beautiful; that bodes ill—and she already has a husband.

sentences.zh: 」帝密令人殺其夫而納之，生紹，終致大逆焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor secretly had her husband killed and took her; she bore Shao, and in the end brought great treason.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor secretly had her husband killed and took her in. She bore Shao—and in the end brought great treason upon the house.

sentences.zh: 陽平王熙，天興六年封，聰達有雅操。

translations.literal: Prince of Yangping Xi was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing; clever and accomplished, with refined conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yangping, Xi, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing. Clever and accomplished, he bore himself with refined conduct.

sentences.zh: 明元練兵於東部，詔熙督十二軍校閱，甚得軍儀，賞賜隆厚。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan drilled troops in the eastern regions he ordered Xi to supervise twelve armies in review; he won great military bearing and received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan drilled troops in the eastern regions he ordered Xi to supervise twelve armies in review. Xi displayed excellent military bearing and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 泰常六年，薨，帝哀慟不已。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taichang he died; the emperor mourned without end.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taichang he died, and the emperor mourned without cease.

sentences.zh: 長子佗襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Tuo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 佗性忠厚，武藝無過者。

translations.literal: Tuo was honest and generous; in martial arts he had no peer.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was honest and generous, though in martial skill he had no outstanding peer.

sentences.zh: 後改封淮南王，鎮武牢，威名甚著。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed to Prince of Huainan; he guarded Wulao and his renown was great.
translations.idiomatic: Later his fief was changed to Prince of Huainan. He guarded Wulao, and his renown was great.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，位司徒，賜安車几杖，入朝不趨。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he held the post of Minister of State and was granted a carriage, staff, and table; he need not hurry when entering court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he served as Minister of State and was granted a carriage, staff, and table; he need not hurry when entering court.

sentences.zh: 太和十二年，薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taihe he died.

sentences.zh: 時孝文有事太廟，始薦，聞之，廢祭，輿駕親臨哀慟，禮賵有加，諡曰靖王。

translations.literal: Xiaowen was then occupied with the Imperial Ancestor Temple and had just begun the offering; hearing of it he canceled the rite, went in person to mourn with deep grief, and added to the funeral gifts—posthumous title Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen was then occupied with the Imperial Ancestor Temple and had just begun the offering. Hearing of Tuo's death he canceled the rite, went in person to mourn with deep grief, and added to the funeral gifts. He was posthumously titled Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 世子吐萬早卒。

translations.literal: His heir Tuwán died early.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Tuwán died young.

sentences.zh: 子僖王顯襲祖爵，薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Xi Xian inherited the grandfather's title and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Xi Xian inherited the grandfather's title and died.

sentences.zh: 子世遵襲。

translations.literal: His son Shizun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizun inherited.

sentences.zh: 孝明時，為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaoming he was Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaoming he served as Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 在邊境，前代以來，互相抄掠，世遵到州，不聽侵擾。

translations.literal: On the frontier, generation after generation, raids and counter-raids had been the rule; when Shizun reached the province he forbade harassment.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier, generation after generation, raids and counter-raids had been the rule. When Shizun reached the province he forbade harassment.

sentences.zh: 其弟均時在荊州，為朝陽戍主。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jun was then in Jing Province as commandant of Chaoyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jun was then in Jing Province as commandant of Chaoyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 有南戍主妻，三月三日遊戲沔水側，均輒遣部曲掠取。

translations.literal: A southern garrison commandant's wife, on the third day of the third month, was playing along the Mian River; Jun sent his troops to seize her.
translations.idiomatic: A southern garrison commandant's wife, on the third day of the third month, was playing along the Mian River; Jun sent his troops to seize her.

sentences.zh: 世遵聞之，責均，遂移還本戍，吳人感荷。

translations.literal: Shizun heard of it, rebuked Jun, and had him transferred back to his original garrison; the Wu people were deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Shizun heard of it, rebuked Jun, and had him transferred back to his original garrison. The Wu people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 後頗行貨賄，散費邊儲，是以聲名有損。

translations.literal: Later he took to bribery and squandered frontier stores, and so his reputation suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took to bribery and squandered frontier stores, and his reputation suffered.

sentences.zh: 薨于定州刺史，諡曰康王。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of Ding Province; posthumous title Prince Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Governor of Ding Province and was posthumously titled Prince Kang.

sentences.zh: 吐萬弟鐘葵，早卒。

translations.literal: Tuwán's younger brother Zhongkui died early.
translations.idiomatic: Tuwán's younger brother Zhongkui died young.

sentences.zh: 長子法壽，累遷安州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fashou rose repeatedly to Governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fashou rose repeatedly to Governor of An Province.

sentences.zh: 法壽先令所親，微服入境，觀察風俗。

translations.literal: Before taking office Fashou sent trusted men in disguise across the border to observe local customs.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office Fashou sent trusted men in disguise across the border to observe local customs.

sentences.zh: 下車便大行賞罰，於是境內肅然。

translations.literal: On taking his post he at once carried out great rewards and punishments, and the territory became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On taking his post he at once carried out stern rewards and punishments, and the territory became orderly.

sentences.zh: 後於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: Later he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 子慶智，性貪鄙。

translations.literal: His son Qingzhi was greedy and base.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingzhi was greedy and base.

sentences.zh: 為太尉主簿，事無大小，得物然後判，或十數錢，或二十錢，得便取之，府中號為「十錢主簿。」

translations.literal: As chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, on matters great or small he would judge only after receiving something—ten or twenty coins—and take it on the spot; the office called him "Chief Clerk of Ten Coins."
translations.idiomatic: As chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, on matters great or small he would judge only after receiving something—ten or twenty coins—and pocket it on the spot. The office called him "Chief Clerk of Ten Coins."

sentences.zh: 法壽弟法僧，位益州刺史，殺戮自任，威怒無恆。

translations.literal: Fashou's younger brother Faseng held the post of Governor of Yi Province; he killed at will and his wrath knew no constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou's younger brother Faseng served as Governor of Yi Province. He killed at will and his wrath knew no constancy.

sentences.zh: 王、賈諸姓，州內人士，法僧皆召為卒伍，無所假縱。

translations.literal: Wang, Jia, and other surnames of note within the province—Faseng summoned them all as common soldiers and showed no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang, Jia, and other leading families of the province—Faseng summoned them all as common soldiers and showed no indulgence.

sentences.zh: 於是合境皆反，招引外寇。

translations.literal: Then the whole province rose in revolt and called in outside raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Then the whole province rose in revolt and called in outside raiders.

sentences.zh: 後拜徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 法僧本附元叉，以驕恣，恐禍及己，將謀為逆。

translations.literal: Faseng had originally attached himself to Yuan Cha; fearing disaster from his arrogance, he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Faseng had originally attached himself to Yuan Cha. Fearful that his arrogance would bring disaster upon him, he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時領主書兼舍人張文伯奉使徐州，法僧謂曰：「我欲與卿去危就安，能從我否？

translations.literal: At the time Director of Documents and concurrently Gentleman-in-Attendance Zhang Wenbo was on mission to Xu Province; Faseng said to him: "I wish to leave danger for safety with you—will you follow me?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of Documents and concurrently Gentleman-in-Attendance Zhang Wenbo was on mission to Xu Province. Faseng said to him: "I wish to leave danger for safety with you—will you follow me?

sentences.zh: 」文伯曰：「安能棄孝義而從叛逆也！

translations.literal: " Wenbo said: "How could I abandon filial duty and righteousness to follow a rebel!
translations.idiomatic: " Wenbo said: "How could I abandon filial duty and righteousness to follow a rebel!

sentences.zh: 」法僧將殺之，文伯罵曰：「僕甯死見文陵松柏，不能生作背國之虜！

translations.literal: " Faseng was about to kill him; Wenbo cursed: "I would rather die among the cypresses of Wénling than live as a traitor to the state!
translations.idiomatic: " Faseng was about to kill him. Wenbo cursed: "I would rather die among the cypresses of Wénling than live as a traitor to the state!

sentences.zh: 」法僧殺之。

translations.literal: " Faseng killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Faseng killed him.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，法僧殺行台高諒，反于彭城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang Faseng killed the touring commissioner Gao Liang and rebelled at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang Faseng killed the touring commissioner Gao Liang and rebelled at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 自稱尊號，改元天啟。

translations.literal: He styled himself with an honorific title and changed the era name to Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself with an honorific title and changed the era name to Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 大軍致討，法僧奔梁。

translations.literal: When the great army came to punish him, Faseng fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army came to punish him, Faseng fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 其武官三千餘人戍彭城者，法僧皆印額為奴，逼將南度。

translations.literal: More than three thousand military officers garrisoning Pengcheng—Faseng branded their foreheads as slaves and forced them south.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand military officers garrisoning Pengcheng—Faseng branded their foreheads as slaves and forced them south.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝授法僧司空，封始安郡王，尋改封宋王，甚見優寵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Faseng Minister of Works and enfeoffed him Duke of Shian, later changed to Prince of Song, with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Faseng Minister of Works and enfeoffed him Duke of Shian, later changed to Prince of Song, with great favor.

sentences.zh: 又進位太尉，仍立為魏主。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Grand Commandant and set up as ruler of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Commandant and set up as ruler of Wei.

sentences.zh: 不行，授開府儀同三司、郢州刺史，乃徵為太尉。

translations.literal: He would not go; he was appointed Commissioner with the Golden Seal, Minister of Works with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ying Province, then summoned back as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He would not go. He was appointed Commissioner with the Golden Seal, Minister of Works with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ying Province, then summoned back as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒于梁，諡曰襄厲王。

translations.literal: He died in Liang; posthumous title Prince Xiangli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Liang and was posthumously titled Prince Xiangli.

sentences.zh: 子景隆、景仲。

translations.literal: His sons Jinglong and Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jinglong and Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 河南王曜，天興六年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Henan Yao was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Henan, Yao, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.

sentences.zh: 五歲，嘗射雀于道武前，中之，帝驚歎焉。

translations.literal: At five he once shot a sparrow before Daowu and hit it; the emperor marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At five he once shot a sparrow before Daowu and hit it; the emperor marveled.

sentences.zh: 及長，武藝絕人，與陽平王熙等並督諸軍講武，眾咸服其勇。

translations.literal: When grown, his martial arts were unmatched; with Prince of Yangping Xi and others he directed armies in drill, and all submitted to his courage.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, his martial arts were unmatched. With the Prince of Yangping Xi and others he directed armies in drill, and all submitted to his courage.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 長子提襲。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ti inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ti inherited.

sentences.zh: 驍烈有父風，改封潁川王。

translations.literal: Fierce and bold with his father's spirit, his fief was changed to Prince of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and bold with his father's spirit, his fief was changed to Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 迎昭儀於塞北。

translations.literal: He welcomed the Lady of Brilliant Deportment from beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed the Lady of Brilliant Deportment from beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時年十六，有夙成之量，殊域敬焉。

translations.literal: He was then sixteen, with precocious capacity; the frontier peoples revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sixteen, with precocious capacity; the frontier peoples revered him.

sentences.zh: 後改封武昌，累遷統萬鎮都大將，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed to Wuchang; he rose repeatedly to Grand General commanding Tongwan, and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Later his fief was changed to Wuchang. He rose repeatedly to Grand General commanding Tongwan and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰成王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Cheng.

sentences.zh: 長子和，字善意，襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son He, styled Shanyi, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son He, styled Shanyi, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 初，和聘乙氏公主女為妃，生子顯，薄之。

translations.literal: At first He betrothed the daughter of Princess Yi's clan as consort and bore a son Xian, but held her in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: At first He betrothed the daughter of Princess Yi's clan as consort and bore a son Xian, but held her in low regard.

sentences.zh: 以公主故，不得遣出。

translations.literal: Because of the princess he could not send her away.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the princess he could not send her away.

sentences.zh: 因忿，遂自落發為沙門。

translations.literal: In anger he shaved his head and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: In anger he shaved his head and became a monk.

sentences.zh: 既不幸其母，乃舍顯，以爵讓其次弟鑒。

translations.literal: Displeased with his mother as well, he abandoned Xian and yielded the title to his next younger brother Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased with his mother as well, he abandoned Xian and yielded the title to his next younger brother Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒固辭。

translations.literal: Jian firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jian firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 公主以其外孫不得襲爵，訴于孝文。

translations.literal: The princess, because her grandson could not inherit, appealed to Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, because her grandson could not inherit, appealed to Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔鑒終之後，令顯襲爵，鑒乃受之。

translations.literal: Xiaowen decreed that after Jian's death Xian should inherit; Jian then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen decreed that after Jian's death Xian should inherit; Jian then accepted.

sentences.zh: 鑒字紹達，沉重少言，寬和好士。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Shaoda, was grave and sparing of words, generous and fond of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, styled Shaoda, was grave and sparing of words, generous and fond of scholars.

sentences.zh: 為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 時革變之始，鑒上書遵孝文之旨，采齊之舊風。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reforms Jian submitted a memorial following Xiaowen's intent, drawing on Qi customs of old.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reforms Jian submitted a memorial following Xiaowen's intent, drawing on the old customs of Qi.

sentences.zh: 軌制粲然，皆合規矩。

translations.literal: Regulations were set forth in brilliant order, all conforming to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were set forth in brilliant order, all conforming to rule.

sentences.zh: 孝文下詔褒美，班之天下，一如鑒所上。

translations.literal: Xiaowen issued an edict of praise and promulgated it throughout the realm, exactly as Jian had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen issued an edict of praise and promulgated it throughout the realm, exactly as Jian had submitted.

sentences.zh: 齊人愛詠，咸曰耳目更新。

translations.literal: The people of Qi loved to sing of it, all saying their ears and eyes were renewed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi loved to sing of it, all saying their ears and eyes had been renewed.

sentences.zh: 和與鑒子伯崇競求承襲，詔聽和襲，位東郡太守。

translations.literal: He and Jian's son Bochong both pressed to inherit; an edict allowed He to inherit, and he held the post of Governor of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jian's son Bochong both pressed to inherit; an edict allowed He to inherit, and he held the post of Governor of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡人孫天恩家豪富，嘗與和爭地，遣奴客打和垂死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Tian'en of the commandery was a wealthy magnate; he had once disputed land with He, and sent slave retainers who beat He nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Tian'en of the commandery was a wealthy magnate. He had once disputed land with He and sent slave retainers who beat He nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 至此，和誣天恩與北賊來往，父子兄弟一時俱戮，資財田宅皆沒於官。

translations.literal: Now He accused Tian'en and his sons and brothers of trafficking with northern bandits; father, sons, and brothers were executed together, and property, goods, fields, and houses were all confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Now He accused Tian'en and his sons and brothers of trafficking with northern bandits. Father, sons, and brothers were executed together, and property, goods, fields, and houses were all confiscated.

sentences.zh: 天恩宗從欲詣闕訴冤，以和元叉之親，不敢告列。

translations.literal: Tian'en's clansmen wished to go to court to plead injustice, but because He was kin to Yuan Cha they dared not lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'en's clansmen wished to go to court to plead injustice, but because He was kin to Yuan Cha they dared not lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 和語其郡人曰：「我覓一州，亦應可得。

translations.literal: He told men of his commandery: "If I sought a whole province, I could probably get one.
translations.idiomatic: He told men of his commandery: "If I sought a whole province, I could probably get one.

sentences.zh: 念此小人，痛入骨髓，故乞此郡，以報宿怨，此後更不求富貴。

translations.literal: Thinking of this petty man, the pain goes to the marrow—so I begged this commandery to repay an old grudge; after this I will seek no more wealth or rank.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of this petty man, the pain goes to the marrow—so I begged this commandery to repay an old grudge. After this I will seek no more wealth or rank.

sentences.zh: 」識者曰：「王當沒於此矣！

translations.literal: " Men of insight said: "The prince will perish in this place!
translations.idiomatic: " Men of insight said: "The prince will perish in this place!

sentences.zh: 」薨，贈相州刺史。

translations.literal: " He died; posthumously made Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: " He died and was posthumously made Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 河間王修，天賜四年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Xiu was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian, Xiu, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子，太武詔河南王曜子羯兒襲，改封略陽王。

translations.literal: He died without sons; Taiwu decreed that Prince of Henan Yao's son Jie'er should inherit, and his fief was changed to Prince of Lüeyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons. Taiwu decreed that the Prince of Henan Yao's son Jie'er should inherit, and his fief was changed to Prince of Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 正平初，有罪賜死，爵除。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Zhengping he was guilty and granted death; the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning of Zhengping he was guilty and granted death; the title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 長樂王處文，天賜四年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Changle Chuwén was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changle, Chuwén, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 聰辯夙成。

translations.literal: Clever and eloquent from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and eloquent from youth.

sentences.zh: 年十四，薨。

translations.literal: At fourteen he died.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he died.

sentences.zh: 明元悼傷之，自小僉槠至葬，常親臨哀慟。

translations.literal: Mingyuan grieved deeply; from the small coffin of catalpa to the burial he often came in person to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan grieved deeply. From the small catalpa coffin to the burial he often came in person to mourn.

sentences.zh: 陪葬金陵，無子，爵除。

translations.literal: Buried beside Jinling; no sons; title abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried beside Jinling. Having no sons, the title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 廣平王連，天賜四年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Lian was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping, Lian, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子，太武以陽平王熙第二子渾為南平王，以繼連後。

translations.literal: He died without sons; Taiwu made Prince of Yangping Xi's second son Hun Prince of Nanping to continue Lian's line.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons. Taiwu made the Prince of Yangping Xi's second son Hun Prince of Nanping to continue Lian's line.

sentences.zh: 渾好弓馬，射鳥輒曆飛而中之，日射兔得五十頭。

translations.literal: Hun loved bow and horse; shooting birds he would strike them in flight one after another, and in a day shoot fifty hares.
translations.idiomatic: Hun loved bow and horse. Shooting birds he would strike them in flight one after another, and in a day shoot fifty hares.

sentences.zh: 太武嘗命左右分射，勝者中的籌滿，詔渾解之，三發皆中。

translations.literal: Taiwu once ordered attendants to shoot in turns; the winner filled the tally; he ordered Hun to release, and three shots all hit.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu once ordered attendants to shoot in turns; the winner filled the tally. He ordered Hun to release, and three shots all hit.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，器其藝能，常引侍左右。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, valued his skill, and often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, valued his skill, and often kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 累遷涼州鎮將、都督西戎諸軍事、領護西域校尉，恩著涼土。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Commander of Liang Province, Commander-in-Chief of Western Rong, and Colonel Protecting the Western Regions; his grace was felt throughout Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Commander of Liang Province, Commander-in-Chief of Western Rong, and Colonel Protecting the Western Regions; his grace was felt throughout Liang.

sentences.zh: 更滿還京，父老皆涕泣追送，如違所親。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, elders wept and followed to send him off, as if parting from kin.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, elders wept and followed to send him off, as if parting from kin.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子飛襲。

translations.literal: His son Fei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fei inherited.

sentences.zh: 後賜名霄。

translations.literal: Later he was granted the name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted the name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 身長九尺，腰帶十圍，容貌魁偉，雅有風則。

translations.literal: Nine feet tall, a belt ten spans round, imposing in appearance, with refined bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Nine feet tall, a belt ten spans round, imposing in appearance, with refined bearing.

sentences.zh: 貞白卓然，好直言正諫，朝臣憚之。

translations.literal: Upright and pure, he loved straight speech and remonstrance; court ministers feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and pure, he loved straight speech and remonstrance; court ministers feared him.

sentences.zh: 孝文特垂欽重，除宗正卿。

translations.literal: Xiaowen especially favored him and appointed him Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen especially favored him and appointed him Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自今奏事，諸臣相稱，可雲姓名；

translations.literal: An edict said: "From now on in memorials, ministers addressing one another may give their names;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "From now on in memorials, ministers addressing one another may give their names;

sentences.zh: 唯南平王一人，可直言其封。

translations.literal: only the Prince of Nanping alone may speak his title directly.
translations.idiomatic: only the Prince of Nanping alone may speak his title directly.

sentences.zh: 」遷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 薨，賜東園第一秘器。

translations.literal: He died and was granted the first-grade secret coffin of the Eastern Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted the first-grade secret coffin of the Eastern Garden.

sentences.zh: 孝文緦衰臨霄喪，宴不舉樂，諡曰安王。

translations.literal: Xiaowen wore unhemmed mourning at Xiao's funeral, held no banquets, posthumous title Prince An.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen wore unhemmed mourning at Xiao's funeral and held no banquets. He was posthumously titled Prince An.

sentences.zh: 子纂襲。

translations.literal: His son Zuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited.

sentences.zh: 京兆王黎，天賜四年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Li was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingzhao, Li, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子吐相襲，改封江陽王。

translations.literal: His son Tuxiang inherited; his fief was changed to Prince of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuxiang inherited; his fief was changed to Prince of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子。

translations.literal: He died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons.

sentences.zh: 獻文以南平王霄第二子繼字世仁為後，襲封江陽王。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen made Prince of Nanping Xiao's second son Ji, styled Shiren, his heir; he inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen made the Prince of Nanping Xiao's second son Ji, styled Shiren, his heir; he inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he served as Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 為家僮取人女為婦妾，又以良人為婢，為御史所彈，坐免官爵。

translations.literal: A household slave took a man's daughter as wife and concubine, and also took free persons as maidservants; the censor impeached him and he was stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave took a man's daughter as wife and concubine, and also took free persons as maidservants. The censor impeached him and he was stripped of office and title.

sentences.zh: 及靈太后臨朝，繼子叉先納太后妹，復繼本封；

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, Ji's son Cha had first taken the dowager's younger sister; Ji recovered his original fief;
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, Ji's son Cha had first taken the dowager's younger sister; Ji recovered his original fief;

sentences.zh: 後徙封京兆王，曆司徒，加侍中。

translations.literal: later his fief was changed to Prince of Jingzhao; he held the posts of Minister of State and was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: later his fief was changed to Prince of Jingzhao. He held the posts of Minister of State and was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 繼，孝文時已曆內外顯任，靈太后臨朝，入居心膂，曆轉臺司。

translations.literal: Ji, already holding prominent posts inside and outside under Xiaowen, when Ling came to court entered the inner circle of trust and rose through the high offices.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, already holding prominent posts inside and outside under Xiaowen, when Ling came to court entered the inner circle of trust and rose through the high offices.

sentences.zh: 頻表遜位，轉太保，侍中如故，加前後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to yield his post, was transferred to Grand Guardian, Palace Attendant as before, with drums before and behind added.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized to yield his post, was transferred to Grand Guardian, Palace Attendant as before, with drums before and behind added.

sentences.zh: 詔以至節，禮有朝慶，繼位高年宿，可依齊郡王簡故事，朝訖引坐，免其拜伏。

translations.literal: An edict said that at the great festivals, when rites require court celebration, Ji by his high rank and long years might follow the precedent of Prince of Qijun Jian—after court he was led to sit, exempt from bowing and prostration.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said that at the great festivals, when rites require court celebration, Ji by his high rank and long years might follow the precedent of Prince of Qijun Jian—after court he was led to sit, exempt from bowing and prostration.

sentences.zh: 轉太傅，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 時叉執殺生之權，拜受之日，送者傾朝，有識者為之致懼。

translations.literal: At that time Cha held the power of life and death; on the day of Ji's appointment those who escorted him filled the court, and men of insight were afraid for him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cha held the power of life and death. On the day of Ji's appointment those who escorted him filled the court, and men of insight were afraid for him.

sentences.zh: 又詔令乘步挽至殿廷，兩人扶侍，禮與丞相高陽王埒。

translations.literal: Another edict allowed him to ride in a hand-drawn carriage to the hall, two men supporting him, ceremony equal to the Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict allowed him to ride in a hand-drawn carriage to the hall, two men supporting him, ceremony equal to the Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 後除使持節、侍中、太師、大將軍、錄尚書事、大都督、節度西道諸軍事。

translations.literal: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander, and Commander of Western Route Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander, and Commander of Western Route Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及出師，車駕臨餞，傾朝祖送。

translations.literal: When the army set out the emperor came to feast him; the whole court saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the army set out the emperor came to feast him; the whole court saw him off.

sentences.zh: 尋加太尉公。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional title Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及班師，繼啟求還復封江陽，詔從之。

translations.literal: When the army returned Ji memorialized asking to restore the fief of Jiangyang; the edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned Ji memorialized asking to restore the fief of Jiangyang; the edict assented.

sentences.zh: 繼晚更貪婪，牧守令長新除赴官，無不受納貨賄，以相託付。

translations.literal: In his later years Ji grew greedier; governors, prefects, and magistrates newly appointed to office—all received his bribes as entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Ji grew greedier. Governors, prefects, and magistrates newly appointed to office—all received his bribes as entrustment.

sentences.zh: 妻子各別請屬，至乃郡縣微吏，亦不獲平心選舉。

translations.literal: Wife and sons each made separate requests; even clerks of commanderies and counties could not choose fairly.
translations.idiomatic: Wife and sons each made separate requests; even clerks of commanderies and counties could not choose fairly.

sentences.zh: 憑叉威勢，法官不敢糾擿，天下患之。

translations.literal: Relying on Cha's power, judicial officers dared not investigate; the realm suffered under it.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on Cha's power, judicial officers dared not investigate; the realm suffered under it.

sentences.zh: 叉黜，繼廢於家。

translations.literal: When Cha was dismissed, Ji was confined at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha was dismissed, Ji was confined at home.

sentences.zh: 初，爾硃榮之為直寢，數以名馬奉叉，叉接以恩意，榮甚德之。

translations.literal: At first, when Erzhu Rong was in the Direct Attendance, he several times presented famous horses to Cha; Cha received him with favor, and Rong was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Erzhu Rong was in the Direct Attendance, he several times presented famous horses to Cha. Cha received him with favor, and Rong was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 建義初，復以繼為太師、司州牧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was again made Ji's Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was again made Ji's Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 永安元年，薨，贈假黃鉞都督九州諸軍，錄尚書事、大丞相如故，諡曰武烈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yong'an he died; posthumously granted the golden axe, Commander of Nine Provinces, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Chancellor as before—posthumous title Prince Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yong'an he died. He was posthumously granted the golden axe, Commander of Nine Provinces, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Chancellor as before—posthumous title Prince Wulie.

sentences.zh: 叉字伯俊，小字夜叉。

translations.literal: Cha, styled Bojun, childhood name Yecha.
translations.idiomatic: Cha, styled Bojun, childhood name Yecha.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，以叉妹夫，除通直郎。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, as Cha's brother-in-law he was made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, as Cha's brother-in-law he was made Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 叉妻封新平君，後遷馮翊君，拜女侍中。

translations.literal: Cha's wife was enfeoffed Lady of Xinping, later Lady of Fengyi, and made Lady Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's wife was enfeoffed Lady of Xinping, later Lady of Fengyi, and made Lady Attendant of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 叉女夭，靈太后詔贈鄉主。

translations.literal: Cha's daughter died young; Ling issued an edict enfeoffing her as District Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's daughter died young; Ling issued an edict enfeoffing her as District Lady.

sentences.zh: 叉累加侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Cha was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 既在門下，兼總禁兵，深為靈太后所信委。

translations.literal: Once in the Gate Department he also held overall command of the forbidden troops and was deeply trusted by Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the Gate Department he also held overall command of the forbidden troops and was deeply trusted by Ling.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌以親賢輔政，每欲斥黜之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, as a kinsman and worthy man assisting in government, often wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, as a kinsman and worthy man assisting in government, often wished to remove him.

sentences.zh: 叉遂令通直郎宋維，告司染都尉韓文殊欲謀逆立懌，懌坐禁止。

translations.literal: Cha then had Regular Attendant Song Wei report that Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu plotted treason to set up Yi; Yi was confined.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then had Regular Attendant Song Wei report that Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu plotted treason to set up Yi. Yi was confined.

sentences.zh: 後窮案無實，懌雖得免，猶以兵衛守于宮西別館。

translations.literal: Later exhaustive investigation found no truth; though Yi was released he was still guarded by troops in a separate lodge west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later exhaustive investigation found no truth. Though Yi was released he was still guarded by troops in a separate lodge west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，叉恐懌終為己害，乃與侍中劉騰密謀，詐取主食中黃門胡度、胡定列，誣懌云：「貨度等金帛，令以毒藥置禦食中以害帝。

translations.literal: After a long while Cha feared Yi would in the end harm him; with Palace Attendant Liu Teng he secretly plotted, falsely taking the chief food-service eunuchs Hu Du and Hu Ding to accuse Yi: "He bribed Du and others with gold and silk to place poison in the imperial food to harm the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Cha feared Yi would in the end harm him. With Palace Attendant Liu Teng he secretly plotted, falsely taking the chief food-service eunuchs Hu Du and Hu Ding to accuse Yi: "He bribed Du and others with gold and silk to place poison in the imperial food to harm the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」騰以具奏。

translations.literal: " Teng memorialized with the full report.
translations.idiomatic: " Teng memorialized with the full report.

sentences.zh: 明帝信之，乃禦顯陽殿。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming believed it; he then held court at Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming believed it; he then held court at Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 騰閉永巷門，靈太后不得出。

translations.literal: Teng closed the Eternal Lane gate; the empress dowager could not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Teng closed the Eternal Lane gate; the empress dowager could not go out.

sentences.zh: 懌入，遇叉于含章殿后，命宗士及直齋執懌衣袂，將入含章東省。

translations.literal: Yi entered and met Cha behind Hanzhang Hall; he ordered clan guards and direct attendants to seize Yi's sleeves and bring him into the eastern office of Hanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi entered and met Cha behind Hanzhang Hall. He ordered clan guards and direct attendants to seize Yi's sleeves and bring him into the eastern office of Hanzhang.

sentences.zh: 騰稱詔集公卿議，以大逆論。

translations.literal: Teng claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to discuss, charging great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Teng claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to discuss, charging great treason.

sentences.zh: 咸畏叉，無敢異者。

translations.literal: All feared Cha and none dared dissent.
translations.idiomatic: All feared Cha and none dared dissent.

sentences.zh: 唯僕射游肇執意不同。

translations.literal: Only Vice Director You Zhao held a different view.
translations.idiomatic: Only Vice Director You Zhao held a different view.

sentences.zh: 叉、騰持公卿議入奏，夜中殺懌。

translations.literal: Cha and Teng took the ministers' discussion in to memorialize; in the middle of the night Yi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cha and Teng took the ministers' discussion in to memorialize; in the middle of the night Yi was killed.

sentences.zh: 於是假為靈太后辭遜詔，叉遂與太師、高陽王雍等輔政。

translations.literal: Then they forged an edict in the empress dowager's name yielding power; Cha then with Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong and others assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: Then they forged an edict in the empress dowager's name yielding power. Cha then with Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong and others assisted in government.

sentences.zh: 常直禁中，明帝呼為姨父。

translations.literal: He constantly attended in the forbidden quarters; Ming called him Uncle by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly attended in the forbidden quarters; Ming called him Uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 自後百寮重跡。

translations.literal: After that the hundred officials trod on one another's heels.
translations.idiomatic: After that the hundred officials trod on one another's heels.

sentences.zh: 後帝徙禦徽音殿，叉亦入居殿右，曲盡佞媚，遂出入禁中，恆令勇士持刀劍以自先後。

translations.literal: Later the emperor moved to Huiyin Hall; Cha also dwelt on the hall's right, flattering to the utmost, and went in and out of the forbidden quarters, always having brave men carry swords before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor moved to Huiyin Hall; Cha also dwelt on the hall's right, flattering to the utmost, and went in and out of the forbidden quarters, always having brave men carry swords before and behind.

sentences.zh: 叉於千秋門外廠下施木闌檻，有時出入，止息其中，腹心防守，以備竊發。

translations.literal: Cha set wooden railings in the shed outside the Qianqiu Gate; when he went in or out he would rest there, with trusted guards against sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cha set wooden railings in the shed outside the Qianqiu Gate. When he went in or out he would rest there, with trusted guards against sudden attack.

sentences.zh: 初，叉之專政，矯情自飾，勞謙待士。

translations.literal: At first, when Cha held sole power, he feigned sentiment and adorned himself, laboring humbly to treat scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Cha held sole power, he feigned sentiment and adorned himself, laboring humbly to treat scholars.

sentences.zh: 得志之後，便自驕愎，耽酒好色，與奪任情。

translations.literal: Once he had his wish he turned arrogant and willful, addicted to wine and women, seizing and granting at whim.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had his wish he turned arrogant and willful, addicted to wine and women, seizing and granting at whim.

sentences.zh: 乃於禁中自作別庫掌握之，珍寶充牣其中。

translations.literal: He made a separate treasury in the forbidden quarters and held it himself; treasures filled it.
translations.idiomatic: He made a separate treasury in the forbidden quarters and held it himself; treasures filled it.

sentences.zh: 叉曾臥婦人於食輿，以晄巴覆之。

translations.literal: Cha once had a woman lie in the food carriage covered with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Cha once had a woman lie in the food carriage covered with a quilt.

sentences.zh: 輿入禁內，出亦如之，直衛雖知，莫敢言者。

translations.literal: The carriage entered the inner quarters and left the same way; the guards knew but none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage entered the inner quarters and left the same way. The guards knew but none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 姑姊婦女，朋淫無別。

translations.literal: Aunts, elder and younger sisters, and women—promiscuity without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Aunts, elder and younger sisters, and women—promiscuity without distinction.

sentences.zh: 政事怠墮，綱紀不舉。

translations.literal: Government affairs languished; discipline was not upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Government affairs languished; discipline was not upheld.

sentences.zh: 州鎮多非其人，於是天下遂亂矣。

translations.literal: Many provinces and garrisons had unfit men in office; then the realm fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Many provinces and garrisons had unfit men in office; then the realm fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 叉自知不法，恐被廢黜，乃陰遣弟洪業召武州人姬庫根等與之聚宴。

translations.literal: Cha knew himself unlawful and feared dismissal; he secretly sent his younger brother Hongye to summon men of Wu Province such as Ji Kugen to feast with him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha knew himself unlawful and feared dismissal. He secretly sent his younger brother Hongye to summon men of Wu Province such as Ji Kugen to feast with him.

sentences.zh: 遂為誓盟，欲令為亂，朝廷必以己為大將軍往伐，因以共為表裏，如此可得自立。

translations.literal: They swore an oath, intending to stir rebellion so the court would surely appoint him Grand General to campaign; they would then act inside and outside together and so establish himself.
translations.idiomatic: They swore an oath, intending to stir rebellion so the court would surely appoint him Grand General to campaign. They would then act inside and outside together and so establish himself.

sentences.zh: 根等然其言，乃厚遺根等，遣還州，與洪業買馬。

translations.literal: Kugen and the rest agreed; he richly rewarded Kugen and the rest and sent them back to the province to buy horses with Hongye.
translations.idiomatic: Kugen and the rest agreed. He richly rewarded them and sent them back to the province to buy horses with Hongye.

sentences.zh: 從劉騰死後，防衛微緩。

translations.literal: After Liu Teng died the guard grew somewhat slack.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Teng died the guard grew somewhat slack.

sentences.zh: 叉頗亦自寬，時宿於外，每日出遊，留連他邑。

translations.literal: Cha also grew somewhat at ease; he often lodged outside, going out every day to roam and lingering in other districts.
translations.idiomatic: Cha also grew somewhat at ease. He often lodged outside, going out every day to roam and lingering in other districts.

sentences.zh: 靈太后微察知之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling subtly detected it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling subtly detected it.

sentences.zh: 正光五年秋，靈太后對明帝謂群臣，求出家於嵩山閒居寺，欲自下發。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang Ling told Ming and the ministers she wished to leave the world for Xianju Temple on Mount Song and to shave her own head.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang Ling told Ming and the ministers she wished to leave the world for Xianju Temple on Mount Song and to shave her own head.

sentences.zh: 帝與群臣大懼，叩頭泣涕。

translations.literal: The emperor and ministers were greatly afraid and kowtowed weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and ministers were greatly afraid and kowtowed weeping.

sentences.zh: 遂與太后密謀圖之。

translations.literal: They then secretly plotted with the dowager against him.
translations.idiomatic: They then secretly plotted with the dowager against him.

sentences.zh: 乃對叉流涕，敘太后欲出家憂怖之心。

translations.literal: They then wept before Cha and told of the dowager's wish to leave the world and her fearful heart.
translations.idiomatic: They then wept before Cha and told of the dowager's wish to leave the world and her fearful heart.

sentences.zh: 叉乃勸帝從太后意。

translations.literal: Cha then urged the emperor to follow the dowager's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then urged the emperor to follow the dowager's wish.

sentences.zh: 於是太后數禦顯陽，二宮無復禁礙。

translations.literal: Then the dowager often held court at Xianyang; the two palaces were no longer barred.
translations.idiomatic: Then the dowager often held court at Xianyang; the two palaces were no longer barred.

sentences.zh: 舉其親元法僧為徐州刺史，法僧據州反叛。

translations.literal: His kinsman Yuan Faseng was raised to Governor of Xu Province; Faseng held the province and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Yuan Faseng was raised to Governor of Xu Province; Faseng held the province and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 靈太后數以為言，叉深愧悔。

translations.literal: Ling spoke of it repeatedly; Cha was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Ling spoke of it repeatedly; Cha was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 丞相、高陽王雍雖位重於叉，而甚畏憚。

translations.literal: Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang Yong, though higher in rank than Cha, greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang Yong, though higher in rank than Cha, greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 會太后與帝游洛水，遂幸雍第，定圖叉之計。

translations.literal: When the dowager and emperor toured the Luo River they then visited Yong's residence and settled the plan against Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When the dowager and emperor toured the Luo River they then visited Yong's residence and settled the plan against Cha.

sentences.zh: 後雍從帝朝太后，乃進言叉父子權重。

translations.literal: Later Yong followed the emperor to audience with the dowager and advanced the argument that Cha father and son held excessive power.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yong followed the emperor to audience with the dowager and advanced the argument that Cha father and son held excessive power.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「然。

translations.literal: The dowager said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager said: "So it is.

sentences.zh: 元郎若忠於朝廷，何故不去領軍，以餘官輔政？

translations.literal: If Lord Yuan is loyal to the court, why does he not leave command of the guards and assist in government with his other offices?
translations.idiomatic: If Lord Yuan is loyal to the court, why does he not leave command of the guards and assist in government with his other offices?

sentences.zh: 」叉聞之甚懼，免冠求解。

translations.literal: " Cha heard and was greatly afraid; he removed his cap and begged release.
translations.idiomatic: " Cha heard and was greatly afraid. He removed his cap and begged release.

sentences.zh: 乃以叉為儀同三司、尚書令、侍中、領左右。

translations.literal: Cha was then made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Director of the Masters of Writing, Palace Attendant, and Commander of the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was then made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Director of the Masters of Writing, Palace Attendant, and Commander of the Left and Right.

sentences.zh: 叉雖去兵權，然總任內外，不慮黜廢。

translations.literal: Though Cha had lost military power he still held overall charge inside and outside and did not fear dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cha had lost military power he still held overall charge inside and outside and did not fear dismissal.

sentences.zh: 又有閹人張景嵩、劉思逸、屯弘昶、伏景謀廢叉。

translations.literal: Also eunuchs Zhang Jingsong, Liu Siyi, Tun Hongchang, and Fu Jing plotted to depose Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Also eunuchs Zhang Jingsong, Liu Siyi, Tun Hongchang, and Fu Jing plotted to depose Cha.

sentences.zh: 嵩以帝嬪潘外憐有幸，說雲，元叉欲害之。

translations.literal: Song, because the emperor's consort Pan Wailian was favored, told Yun that Yuan Cha wished to harm her.
translations.idiomatic: Song, because the emperor's consort Pan Wailian was favored, told Yun that Yuan Cha wished to harm her.

sentences.zh: 嬪泣訴於帝云：「叉非直欲殺妾，亦將害陛下。

translations.literal: The consort wept and told the emperor: "Cha does not only wish to kill me—he will also harm Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The consort wept and told the emperor: "Cha does not only wish to kill me—he will also harm Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝信之。

translations.literal: " The emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor believed it.

sentences.zh: 後叉出宿，遂解其侍中。

translations.literal: Later when Cha lodged outside they removed his Palace Attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Cha lodged outside they removed his Palace Attendant post.

sentences.zh: 旦欲入宮，門者不納。

translations.literal: At dawn he wished to enter the palace; the gatekeepers would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he wished to enter the palace; the gatekeepers would not admit him.

sentences.zh: 尋除名。

translations.literal: Soon he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 初，咸陽王禧以逆見誅，其子樹，梁封為鄴王。

translations.literal: At first Prince of Xianyang Xi was executed for treason; his son Shu, Liang enfeoffed as Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At first Prince of Xianyang Xi was executed for treason; his son Shu, Liang enfeoffed as Prince of Ye.

sentences.zh: 及法僧反叛後，樹遺公卿百寮書，暴叉過惡，言：「叉本名夜叉，弟羅實名羅刹。

translations.literal: After Faseng rebelled Shu sent a letter to the hundred officials exposing Cha's crimes, saying: "Cha's original name is Yecha; his younger brother Luo's true name is Luosha.
translations.idiomatic: After Faseng rebelled Shu sent a letter to the hundred officials exposing Cha's crimes, saying: "Cha's original name is Yecha; his younger brother Luo's true name is Luosha.

sentences.zh: 夜叉、羅刹，此鬼食人，非遇黑風，事同飄墮。

translations.literal: Yecha and Luosha—these demons devour men; unless you meet a black wind you fall like blown leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Yecha and Luosha—these demons devour men. Unless you meet a black wind you fall like blown leaves.

sentences.zh: 鳴呼魏境！

translations.literal: Alas, Wei territory!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Wei territory!

sentences.zh: 離此二災。

translations.literal: Keep far from these two disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Keep far from these two disasters.

sentences.zh: 惡木盜泉，不息不飲，勝名梟稱，不入不為。

translations.literal: Evil tree, stolen spring—do not rest, do not drink; a name surpassing the owl—do not enter, do not become.
translations.idiomatic: Evil tree, stolen spring—do not rest, do not drink; a name surpassing the owl—do not enter, do not become.

sentences.zh: 況昆季此名，表能噬物，日露久矣，始信斯言。

translations.literal: How much more when brothers bear such names, showing they can devour—exposed so long, one finally believes the saying.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when brothers bear such names, showing they can devour—exposed so long, one finally believes the saying.

sentences.zh: 」叉為遠近所惡如此。

translations.literal: " Cha was hated near and far like this.
translations.idiomatic: " Cha was hated near and far like this.

sentences.zh: 其後靈太后顧謂侍臣曰：「劉騰、元叉昔邀朕索鐵券，望得不死，朕賴不與。

translations.literal: Later Ling said to attendants: "Liu Teng and Yuan Cha once begged me for an iron certificate, hoping not to die; I relied on not giving it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ling said to attendants: "Liu Teng and Yuan Cha once begged me for an iron certificate, hoping not to die. I relied on not giving it.

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人韓子順對曰：「臣聞殺活，豈計與否。

translations.literal: " Central Secretariat Attendant Han Zishun replied: "Your servant hears that killing and sparing do not depend on giving or not.
translations.idiomatic: " Central Secretariat Attendant Han Zishun replied: "Your servant hears that killing and sparing do not depend on giving or not.

sentences.zh: 陛下昔雖不與，何解今日不殺？

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty did not give then, why not kill today?
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty did not give then, why not kill today?

sentences.zh: 」靈太后憮然。

translations.literal: " Ling was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Ling was displeased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有人告叉及其弟爪謀反。

translations.literal: Before long someone reported that Cha and his younger brother Zhao plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone reported that Cha and his younger brother Zhao plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 先遣其從弟洪業率六鎮降戶反定州；

translations.literal: First he sent his cousin Hongye to lead surrendered households of the six garrisons to rebel at Ding Province;
translations.idiomatic: First he sent his cousin Hongye to lead surrendered households of the six garrisons to rebel at Ding Province;

sentences.zh: 叉令勾魯陽諸蠻侵擾伊闕，叉兄弟為內應，起有日矣，得其手書。

translations.literal: Cha ordered Gou of Luyang and various tribes to harass Yique; Cha and his brothers were inside accomplices—the day was set; they obtained his handwriting.
translations.idiomatic: Cha ordered Gou of Luyang and various tribes to harass Yique. Cha and his brothers were inside accomplices—the day was set; they obtained his handwriting.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以妹婿故，未忍便決。

translations.literal: Ling, because he was her sister's husband, could not bear to decide at once.
translations.idiomatic: Ling, because he was her sister's husband, could not bear to decide at once.

sentences.zh: 群臣固執不已，明帝又以為言，太后乃從之。

translations.literal: The ministers pressed without cease; Ming also spoke; the dowager then assented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed without cease; Ming also spoke; the dowager then assented.

sentences.zh: 於是叉及弟爪並賜死於家。

translations.literal: Then Cha and his younger brother Zhao were granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Then Cha and his younger brother Zhao were granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 太后猶以妹故，復追贈尚書令、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: The dowager still because of her sister posthumously restored him Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager still because of her sister posthumously restored him Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 叉子舒，秘書郎。

translations.literal: Cha's son Shu was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's son Shu was Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 叉死後，亡奔梁，官至征北大將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: After Cha died he fled to Liang and rose to Grand General Conquering the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Cha died he fled to Liang and rose to Grand General Conquering the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces.

sentences.zh: 子善，亦名善住。

translations.literal: His son Shan, also called Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shan, also called Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 少隨父至江南，性好學，通涉《五經》，尤明《左氏傳》。

translations.literal: Young he followed his father to the south; fond of learning, versed in the Five Classics, especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Young he followed his father to the south. Fond of learning, he was versed in the Five Classics and especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，善歸周，武帝甚禮之，以為太子宮尹，賜爵江陽縣公，每執經以授太子。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing Shan returned to Zhou; Emperor Wu greatly honored him, made him Tutor of the Crown Prince's Palace, enfeoffed Duke of Jiangyang, and often lectured on the classics to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Hou Jing Shan returned to Zhou. Emperor Wu greatly honored him, made him Tutor of the Crown Prince's Palace, enfeoffed Duke of Jiangyang, and often lectured on the classics to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，拜內史侍郎，凡有敷奏，詞氣抑揚，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; whatever he memorialized, the tone rose and fell, and watchers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat. Whatever he memorialized, the tone rose and fell, and watchers fixed their eyes on him.

sentences.zh: 陳使袁雅來聘，上令善就館受書。

translations.literal: Chen envoy Yuan Ya came on embassy; the emperor ordered Shan to go to the lodge to receive the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Chen envoy Yuan Ya came on embassy; the emperor ordered Shan to go to the lodge to receive the letter.

sentences.zh: 雅出門不拜。

translations.literal: Ya went out the door without bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Ya went out the door without bowing.

sentences.zh: 善論舊事有拜之儀，雅未能對。

translations.literal: Shan argued that by old custom there was a bowing rite; Ya could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Shan argued that by old custom there was a bowing rite; Ya could not answer.

sentences.zh: 遂拜，成禮而去。

translations.literal: He then bowed and left with the rite complete.
translations.idiomatic: He then bowed and left with the rite complete.

sentences.zh: 後遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 上嘗親臨釋奠，令善講《孝經》，於是敷陳義理，兼之以諫。

translations.literal: The emperor once came in person to the libation ceremony and ordered Shan to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; he then set forth the meaning and also offered remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once came in person to the libation ceremony and ordered Shan to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety. He then set forth the meaning and also offered remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上大悅曰：「聞江陽之說，更起朕心。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "Hearing Jiangyang's discourse has renewed my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "Hearing Jiangyang's discourse has renewed my heart.

sentences.zh: 」齎絹一百匹，衣一襲。

translations.literal: " He was given a hundred bolts of silk and one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given a hundred bolts of silk and one suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: 善之通博，在何妥之下，然以風流醖藉，俯仰可觀，音韻清朗，由是為後進所歸。

translations.literal: Shan's breadth was below He Tuo, yet by graceful bearing he was pleasing to behold, his voice clear—thus later scholars looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's breadth was below He Tuo, yet by graceful bearing he was pleasing to behold, his voice clear—thus later scholars looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 妥每懷不平，心欲屈善，因講《春秋》。

translations.literal: Tuo always nursed resentment and wished to humble Shan; he therefore lectured on the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo always nursed resentment and wished to humble Shan; he therefore lectured on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 初發題，諸儒畢集，善私謂妥曰：「名望已定，幸無相苦。

translations.literal: When the topic was first announced all the Confucians gathered; Shan privately told Tuo: "Reputation is already settled—please do not press me hard.
translations.idiomatic: When the topic was first announced all the Confucians gathered. Shan privately told Tuo: "Reputation is already settled—please do not press me hard.

sentences.zh: 」妥然之。

translations.literal: " Tuo agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Tuo agreed.

sentences.zh: 及就講肆，妥遂引古今滯義以難善，多不能對。

translations.literal: When they came to the lecture hall Tuo then cited obscure points from antiquity to challenge Shan; he often could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to the lecture hall Tuo then cited obscure points from antiquity to challenge Shan; he often could not answer.

sentences.zh: 二人由是有隙。

translations.literal: From this the two had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: From this the two had a rift.

sentences.zh: 善以高熲有宰相之具，嘗言於上曰：「楊素粗疏，蘇威怯懦，元胄、元旻，正似鴨耳。

translations.literal: Shan, because Gao Feng had the makings of a prime minister, once told the emperor: "Yang Su is coarse, Su Wei timid, Yuan Zhou and Yuan Min are like ducks.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, because Gao Feng had the makings of a prime minister, once told the emperor: "Yang Su is coarse, Su Wei timid, Yuan Zhou and Yuan Min are like ducks.

sentences.zh: 可以付社稷者，唯獨高熲。

translations.literal: He alone to whom the altars may be entrusted is Gao Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He alone to whom the altars may be entrusted is Gao Feng.

sentences.zh: 」上初然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor at first agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at first agreed.

sentences.zh: 及熲得罪，上以善言為熲遊說，深責望之。

translations.literal: When Feng was punished the emperor took Shan's words as lobbying for Feng and blamed him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng was punished the emperor took Shan's words as lobbying for Feng and blamed him deeply.

sentences.zh: 善憂懼，先患消渴，於是病頓而卒。

translations.literal: Shan grew anxious and fearful; he had long suffered from wasting thirst, and now fell ill and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Shan grew anxious and fearful. He had long suffered from wasting thirst, and now fell ill and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 叉弟羅，字仲綱。

translations.literal: Cha's younger brother Luo, styled Zhonggang.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's younger brother Luo, styled Zhonggang.

sentences.zh: 雖父兄貴盛，而虛己接物。

translations.literal: Though father and brothers were noble and flourishing he humbled himself in receiving others.
translations.idiomatic: Though father and brothers were noble and flourishing he humbled himself in receiving others.

sentences.zh: 累遷青州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 叉當朝專政，羅望傾四海，于時才名之士王元景、邢子才、季獎等咸為其賓客，從遊青土。

translations.literal: When Cha held court and sole power Luo's fame tilted the four seas; at the time men of talent and name such as Wang Yuanjing, Xing Zicai, and Ji Jiang were all his guests and traveled with him in Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha held court and sole power Luo's fame tilted the four seas. At the time men of talent and name such as Wang Yuanjing, Xing Zicai, and Ji Jiang were all his guests and traveled with him in Qing.

sentences.zh: 罷州，入為守正卿。

translations.literal: Leaving office he entered as Defender of Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he entered as Defender of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 叉死後，羅通叉妻，時人穢之，或云其救命之計也。

translations.literal: After Cha died Luo took Cha's wife; men of the time reviled it, some saying it was a plan to save his life.
translations.idiomatic: After Cha died Luo took Cha's wife; men of the time reviled it, some saying it was a plan to save his life.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，位尚書令、開府儀同三司、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he held Director of the Masters of Writing, Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he held Director of the Masters of Writing, Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，梁遣將圍逼，羅以州降，封南郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing Liang sent generals to press the siege; Luo surrendered the province and was enfeoffed Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaojing Liang sent generals to press the siege. Luo surrendered the province and was enfeoffed Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 及侯景自立，以羅為開府儀同三司、尚書令，改封江陽王。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing declared himself independent he made Luo Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes and Director of the Masters of Writing, changed his fief to Prince of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing declared himself independent he made Luo Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes and Director of the Masters of Writing, and changed his fief to Prince of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝滅景，周文帝求羅，遂得還。

translations.literal: When Liang Emperor Yuan destroyed Jing, Zhou Emperor Wen sought Luo and he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Emperor Yuan destroyed Jing, Zhou Emperor Wen sought Luo and he was able to return.

sentences.zh: 除開府儀同三司、侍中、少師，襲爵江陽王。

translations.literal: He was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, Junior Preceptor, and inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, Junior Preceptor, and inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 舒子善住，在後從南入關，羅乃以爵還善住，改封羅為固道郡公。

translations.literal: Shu's son Shanshan, following later, entered the pass from the south; Luo then returned the title to Shanshan and Luo was changed to Duke of Gudao.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's son Shanshan, following later, entered the pass from the south. Luo then returned the title to Shanshan and Luo was changed to Duke of Gudao.

sentences.zh: 羅弟爽，字景哲。

translations.literal: Luo's younger brother Shuang, styled Jingzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Luo's younger brother Shuang, styled Jingzhe.

sentences.zh: 少而機警，位給事黃門侍郎、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Clever and alert from youth; he held Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Robe.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and alert from youth, he held Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Robe.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 爽弟蠻，仕齊，歷位兼度支尚書，行潁州事。

translations.literal: Shuang's younger brother Man served Qi and rose to Acting Director of Revenue and acting Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's younger brother Man served Qi and rose to Acting Director of Revenue and acting Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 坐不為繼母服，為左丞所彈。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the Left Director for not wearing mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by the Left Director for not wearing mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 後除開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 齊天保十年，大誅元氏。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qi Tianbao the Yuan clan was greatly slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qi Tianbao the Yuan clan was greatly slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 昭帝元後，蠻之女也，為苦請，自市追免之，賜姓步六孤氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao's Yuan empress was Man's daughter; she pleaded bitterly and bought herself back from the market to be spared; she was granted the surname Buliugu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao's Yuan empress was Man's daughter. She pleaded bitterly and bought herself back from the market to be spared; she was granted the surname Buliugu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 蠻弟爪，字景邕，位給事中，與兄叉同時誅。

translations.literal: Man's younger brother Zhao, styled Jingyong, held Attendant; with his elder brother Cha he was executed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Man's younger brother Zhao, styled Jingyong, held Attendant; with his elder brother Cha he was executed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 繼弟羅侯，遷洛之際，以墳陵在北，遂家于燕州之昌平郡。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Luohou, at the move to Luoyang, because the tombs were in the north settled his household in Changping commandery of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Luohou, at the move to Luoyang, because the tombs were in the north settled his household in Changping commandery of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 內豐資產，唯以意得為適。

translations.literal: Rich within, he did only as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rich within, he did only as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 不入京師，在賓客往來者，必厚相禮遺，豪據北方，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He did not enter the capital; among guests who came and went he always gave lavish gifts and held great renown in the north.
translations.idiomatic: He did not enter the capital. Among guests who came and went he always gave lavish gifts and held great renown in the north.

sentences.zh: 以叉執權，尤不樂入仕，就拜昌平太守。
