translations.literal: Because Cha held power he especially disliked entering office and accepted appointment as Governor of Changping alone.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cha held power he especially disliked entering office and accepted appointment as Governor of Changping alone.

sentences.zh: 明元皇帝七男：杜密皇后生太武皇帝；

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons: the Du Secret Empress bore Emperor Taiwu;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons. The Du Secret Empress bore Emperor Taiwu;

sentences.zh: 大慕容夫人生樂平戾王丕；

translations.literal: the Great Consort Murong bore Prince of Leping Li Pi;
translations.idiomatic: the Great Consort Murong bore the Prince of Leping Li, Pi;

sentences.zh: 安定殤王彌闕母氏；

translations.literal: Prince of Anding Mi—the mother's name is unknown;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Anding Mi—the mother's name is unknown;

sentences.zh: 慕容夫人生樂安宣王範；

translations.literal: Consort Murong bore Prince of Le'an Xuan Fan;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Murong bore the Prince of Le'an Xuan, Fan;

sentences.zh: 尹夫人生永昌莊王健；

translations.literal: Consort Yin bore Prince of Yongchang Zhuang Jian;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yin bore the Prince of Yongchang Zhuang, Jian;

sentences.zh: 建甯王崇、新興王俊二王並闕母氏。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianning Chong and Prince of Xinxing Jun—both mothers unknown.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Jianning Chong and the Prince of Xinxing Jun—both mothers unknown.

sentences.zh: 樂平王丕，少有才幹。

translations.literal: Prince of Leping Pi, in youth had talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Leping, Pi, showed talent and ability from youth.

sentences.zh: 泰常七年封，拜車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taichang he received his fief and was made Grand Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後督河西、高平諸軍討南秦王楊難當。

translations.literal: Later he supervised the armies of Hexi and Gaoping to campaign against the Southern Qin king Yang Nandang.
translations.idiomatic: He later directed the Hexi and Gaoping armies against the Southern Qin king Yang Nandang.

sentences.zh: 軍至略陽，禁令齊肅，所過無私，百姓爭致牛酒。

translations.literal: When the army reached Lueyang, prohibitions were uniformly strict; passing through he took nothing for himself, and the common people vied to offer cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: At Lueyang his discipline was severe and impartial; the people competed to bring him cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 難當懼，還仇池。

translations.literal: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang, in fear, withdrew to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 而諸將議曰：「若不誅豪帥，軍還之後，必聚而為寇。

translations.literal: And the generals deliberated, saying: "If we do not execute the powerful chiefs, after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued: "Unless we kill the local strongmen, they will rally into rebels once we withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」又以大眾遠出，不有所掠，則無以充軍實，賞將士。

translations.literal: Also, with a great host going far out, if they take nothing by plunder there is no way to fill the army's stores and reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, an army this far from home must seize something or it cannot fill its stores and pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 將從之，時中書侍郎高元參丕軍事，諫曰：「今若誅之，是傷其向化之心，恐大軍一還，為亂必速。

translations.literal: The generals were about to follow this; at the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yuan accompanied Pi on campaign affairs and remonstrated, saying: "If we execute them now, this injures their mind of turning to our rule; I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: They were about to agree when Secretariat Attendant Gao Yuan, on Pi's staff, objected: "Slaughter now will destroy their willingness to submit; the moment our main force leaves, revolt will come fast."

sentences.zh: 」丕以為然，於是綏懷初附，秋豪無犯。

translations.literal: Pi thought it correct, and thereupon soothed those newly submitting, not harming even autumn down in passing.
translations.idiomatic: Pi accepted this and pacified the new subjects, harming not even the lightest property.

sentences.zh: 初，馮弘之奔高麗，太武詔遣送之，高麗不遣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Emperor Taiwu issued an edict to have him sent; Goguryeo did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Feng Hong had fled to Goguryeo, Emperor Taiwu ordered him handed over; Goguryeo refused.

sentences.zh: 太武怒，將討之。

translations.literal: Taiwu was angry and was about to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu grew angry and prepared to attack.

sentences.zh: 丕上疏以為和龍新定，宜復之，使廣修農殖，以饒軍實，然後進圖，可一舉而滅。

translations.literal: Pi submitted a memorial considering that with Helong newly pacified, it should be restored, making them broadly cultivate agriculture so as to enrich the army's stores, and then advance plans — they could be destroyed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized that Helong had only just been secured: restore it, expand farming to fill the granaries, then strike — Goguryeo could be taken at one blow.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and dropped the campaign.

sentences.zh: 後坐劉潔事，以憂薨，事在《潔傳》，諡曰戾王。

translations.literal: Later because of the Liu Jie affair he died of grief, the matter is in the Liu Jie biography, posthumous title Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of grief over the Liu Jie affair, treated in Liu Jie's biography; his posthumous name was Li.

sentences.zh: 子拔襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Ba succeeded to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ba inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後坐事賜死，國除。

translations.literal: Later because of an offense he was granted death, the state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for an offense, he was ordered to die and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 丕之薨及日者董道秀之死也，高元遂著《筮論》曰：「昔明元末，起白台，其高二十餘丈。

translations.literal: At Pi's death and the death of the day-augur Dong Daoxiu, Gao Yuan thereupon wrote "On Divination," saying: "Formerly at the end of Emperor Mingyuan, the White Tower was raised, its height more than twenty zhang."
translations.idiomatic: After Pi's death and the execution of the day-augur Dong Daoxiu, Gao Yuan wrote On Divination: "At the end of Emperor Mingyuan's reign a White Tower was built, more than twenty zhang high."

sentences.zh: 樂平王嘗夢登其上，四望無所見。

translations.literal: Prince of Leping once dreamed of climbing atop it, looking in the four directions and seeing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Leping once dreamed he climbed it and looked about on every side but saw nothing.

sentences.zh: 王以問日者董道秀。

translations.literal: The prince asked the day-augur Dong Daoxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked Dong Daoxiu to divine it.

sentences.zh: 筮之，曰：「大吉」。

translations.literal: He divined and said: "Great good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Daoxiu cast the hexagrams and said, "Great good fortune."

sentences.zh: 王默而有喜色。

translations.literal: The prince was silent but had a pleased expression.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said nothing, but his face showed delight.

sentences.zh: 後事發，王遂憂死，而道秀棄市。

translations.literal: Later when the matter broke out, the prince thereupon died in worry, while Daoxiu was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair broke, the prince died in grief; Daoxiu was executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 道秀若推六爻以對王曰：「易稱亢龍有悔。

translations.literal: If Daoxiu had pushed the six lines to answer the prince saying: "The Changes says 'the dragon exalted has regret.'"
translations.idiomatic: Had Daoxiu read the six lines and told the prince, "The Changes says: 'The exalted dragon has regret,'"

sentences.zh: 窮高日亢，高而無人，不為善也。

translations.literal: "Reaching the heights daily exalted, high yet without people — this is not good."
translations.idiomatic: "to rise daily higher, lofty yet without support — that is not auspicious,"

sentences.zh: 」夫如是，則上甯于王，下保於己，福祿方至，豈有禍哉？

translations.literal: If it were thus, then above he would be secure for the prince, below he would preserve himself, fortune and rank would be arriving — how could there be calamity?
translations.idiomatic: then above he would have kept the prince safe, below preserved himself, and fortune would have come — how could disaster follow?

sentences.zh: 今舍於本而從其末，咎釁之至，不亦宜乎！」

translations.literal: Now abandoning the root and following the tip, the arrival of blame and ill omen — is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: But he forsook the root for the branch; blame and ruin came — as they should.

sentences.zh: 安定王彌，泰常七年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Anding Mi, enfeoffed seventh year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anding, Mi, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰殤王。

translations.literal: Died, posthumous title Prince Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Shang.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: Without sons, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 長子良，太武未有子，嘗曰：「兄弟之子猶子。

translations.literal: Eldest son Liang — before Emperor Taiwu had sons, he once said: "A brother's son is like one's own son."
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Liang: before Emperor Taiwu had sons of his own, he said, "A brother's son is as one's own."

sentences.zh: 」親撫養之。

translations.literal: He personally nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Liang himself.

sentences.zh: 長而壯勇多知，嘗參軍國大計。

translations.literal: When grown he was strong and brave with much knowledge, and once participated in great plans of state and army.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, Liang was strong, brave, and well informed, and took part in major state and military decisions.

sentences.zh: 文成時，襲王，拜長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史，為內都大官。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Wencheng he succeeded to the kingship, was appointed Grand General governing Chang'an and Governor of Yongzhou, and served as Inner Metropolitan Official.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he inherited the princedom, became Grand General of Chang'an and Governor of Yongzhou, and served as Inner Metropolitan Official.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰簡王。

translations.literal: Died, posthumous title Prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Jian.

sentences.zh: 建甯王崇，泰常七年封。

translations.literal: Prince Jianning Chong, enfeoffed seventh year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianning, Chong, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 文成時，封崇子麗濟南王。

translations.literal: In the reign of Wencheng, Chong's son Li was enfeoffed Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wencheng, Chong's son Li was made Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 後與京兆王杜元寶謀逆，父子並賜死。

translations.literal: Later he plotted rebellion with Prince of Jingzhao Du Yuanbao; father and son were both granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Later he conspired with Prince of Jingzhao Du Yuanbao; father and son were both ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 新興王俊，泰常七年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Xinxing Jun, enfeoffed seventh year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xinxing, Jun, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，多藝。

translations.literal: In youth skilled at mounted archery, with many arts.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he excelled at mounted archery and had many skills.

sentences.zh: 坐法，削爵為公。

translations.literal: Because of offense his noble title was cut to duke.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense his rank was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 俊好酒色，多越法度。

translations.literal: Jun loved wine and women and often exceeded the bounds of law.
translations.idiomatic: Jun loved wine and women and often broke the law.

sentences.zh: 又以母先遇罪死，而己被貶削，恆懷怨望，頗有悖心。

translations.literal: Also because his mother had earlier met with offense and died, while he himself had been demoted and stripped, he constantly harbored resentment and had quite a rebellious heart.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had earlier been condemned and died; he himself had been demoted. He nursed resentment and a rebellious temper.

sentences.zh: 後事發，賜死，國除。

translations.literal: Later when the matter broke out he was granted death, state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed he was ordered to die and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 子提襲，為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Son Ti succeeded and became Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ti inherited the line and became Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以貪縱削除，加罰，徙配北鎮。

translations.literal: Because of greedy excess his title was cut off, punishment was added, and he was banished to the Northern Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: For greed and license his title was stripped, further penalties imposed, and he was sent to the Northern Garrison.

sentences.zh: 久之，提子員外郎穎免冠請解所居官，代父邊戍，孝文不許。

translations.literal: After long time Ti's son staff attendant Ying removed his cap and requested to resign his post to take his father's place on the frontier — Emperor Xiaowen did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Ti's son Ying, a staff attendant, begged to resign his office and take his father's frontier post; Emperor Xiaowen refused.

sentences.zh: 後昭提從駕南伐。

translations.literal: Later on the southern campaign Ti accompanied the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the southern campaign, Ti accompanied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，參定遷都之議。

translations.literal: At Luoyang he participated in settling the plan to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he took part in deciding the capital transfer.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，以預參遷都功，追封長鄉縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he died; because he had shared in the merit of moving the capital he was posthumously enfeoffed Marquis of Changxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died; for helping move the capital he was posthumously made Marquis of Changxiang.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，贈雍州刺史，諡曰「懿」。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously given Governor of Yongzhou, posthumous title "Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously made Governor of Yongzhou with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 子彧，字文若，紹封。

translations.literal: Son Yu, courtesy name Wenruo, succeeded to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, courtesy name Wenruo, inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 彧少有才學，當時甚美。

translations.literal: Yu in youth had literary talent and at the time was greatly admired.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was gifted in letters from youth and was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光見而謂人曰：「黑頭三公，當此人也。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Guang saw him and said to others: "A dark-haired Three-Dukes — it will be this man."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Guang saw him and said, "Here is a young man who will reach the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 」少與從兄安豐王延明、中山王熙，並以宗室博古文學齊名，時人莫能定其優劣。

translations.literal: In youth together with his cousin Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Zhongshan Xi, all being of the imperial clan with broad learning in the classics and literature equally famous — at the time people could not settle their relative excellence.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his cousins Prince of Anfeng Yanming and Prince of Zhongshan Xi, all imperial clansmen learned in the classics, were equally famed; contemporaries could not rank them.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎范陽盧道將謂吏部清河崔休曰：「三人才學雖並優美，然安豐少於造次，中山皁白太多，未若濟南風流寬雅。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Fan Yang Lu Daojiang said to Personnel Minister Qinghe Cui Xiu: "The three men's learning and talent are all excellent and beautiful, yet Anfeng is lacking in quick repartee, Zhongshan has too much black-and-white distinction, not equal to Jinan's flowing grace and easy elegance."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Lu Daojiang of Fanyang told Personnel Minister Cui Xiu of Qinghe: "All three are brilliant, but Anfeng lacks quick wit, Zhongshan argues too much in black and white — neither matches Jinan's easy grace."

sentences.zh: 」時人為之語曰：「三王楚琳琅，未若濟南備員方。

translations.literal: At the time people made a saying of it: "The three kings are Chu jade, yet not equal to Jinan's full squareness."
translations.idiomatic: People said: "The three princes are Chu jade, but none equals Jinan's completeness."

sentences.zh: 」彧姿制閑裕，吐發流美。

translations.literal: Yu's bearing was leisurely and ample, his utterance flowing and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's manner was relaxed and ample; his speech flowed beautifully.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王誦，有名人也，見之未嘗不心醉忘疲。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Wang Song, a man with a famous name, whenever he saw him never failed to be heart-intoxicated and forget weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Wang Song, a man of renown, never met him without losing himself in delight and forgetting fatigue.

sentences.zh: 奏鄭廟歌詞，時稱其美。

translations.literal: He submitted hymns for the Zheng temple — at the time called beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted temple hymns for the Zheng shrine; they were praised at court.

sentences.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Appointed Palace Attendant Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 彧本名亮，字仕明，時侍中穆紹與彧同署，避紹父諱，啟求改名。

translations.literal: Yu's original given name was Liang, courtesy name Shimming; at the time Attendant-in-ordinary Mu Shao shared office with Yu and to avoid Shao's father's taboo name submitted requesting a name change.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's original name was Liang, courtesy Shimming; Attendant-in-ordinary Mu Shao shared his office and, to avoid Shao's father's taboo, asked that Yu be renamed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「仕明風神運吐，常自以比荀文若，可名彧，以取定體相倫之美。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Shimming's spirit and bearing transport and flow, often comparing himself to Xun Wenruo — may be named Yu, to take the fixed form of equal standing in stature."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Shimming's bearing is lofty and fluent; he compares himself to Xun Yu — let him be named Yu, to match that stature."

sentences.zh: 」彧求復本封，詔許復封臨淮，寄食相州魏郡。

translations.literal: Yu requested restoration of his original fief; edict permitted restoration of Linhuai, provisioned from Xiangzhou Weijun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked to recover his original fief; the court restored Linhuai, with provisions from Weijun in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又長兼御史中尉。

translations.literal: He also long served concurrently as Censor Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He long served concurrently as Censor Commandant.

sentences.zh: 彧以為倫敘得之，不謝。

translations.literal: Yu considered the order of seniority correctly obtained and did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yu thought the appointment proper by seniority and did not decline.

sentences.zh: 領軍於忠忿，言之朝廷曰：「臨淮雖復風流可觀，而無骨鯁之操，中尉之任，恐非所堪。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Yu Zhong was resentful and spoke to the court: "Though Linhuai again has flowing grace to be viewed, he lacks the backbone of firm integrity — the Censor's post, I fear he is not fit for it."
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Yu Zhong, resentful, told the court: "Linhuai may look elegant, but he lacks backbone — I doubt he can bear the censor's office."

sentences.zh: 」遂去威儀，單車而還，朝流為之歎息。

translations.literal: He thereupon removed his insignia, returning in a single cart — the court currents sighed for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu thereupon set aside his insignia and returned in a plain cart; court opinion sighed over him.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、衛將軍、左光祿大夫，兼尚書左僕射，攝選。

translations.literal: Promoted in stages to Attendant-in-ordinary, Guard General, Left Honored Grandee, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, overseeing selection.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attendant-in-ordinary, Guard General, and Left Honored Grandee to concurrent Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, overseeing appointments.

sentences.zh: 後以本官為東道行台。

translations.literal: Later with his original office he became Eastern Route Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Eastern Route Commissioner while keeping his prior offices.

sentences.zh: 會爾硃榮入洛，殺害元氏，彧撫膺慟哭，遂奔梁。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and killed the Yuan clan, Yu beat his breast and wept bitterly, then fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and slaughtered the Yuan, Yu beat his breast and wept, then fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武遣其舍人陳建孫迎接，並觀彧為人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang sent his attendant Chen Jiansun to receive him and also observe Yu's person.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang sent his attendant Chen Jiansun to welcome him and take his measure.

sentences.zh: 建孫稱彧風神閑俊。

translations.literal: Jiansun called Yu's spirit bearing leisurely and handsome.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansun reported that Yu's bearing was easy and handsome.

sentences.zh: 梁武亦先聞名，深相器待。

translations.literal: Wu of Liang had also earlier heard his name and deeply prized and awaited him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor had already heard of him and valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 見彧于樂遊園，因設宴樂。

translations.literal: Seeing Yu at Leyou Garden, thereupon a banquet with music was set.
translations.idiomatic: He received Yu at Leyou Garden and gave a banquet with music.

sentences.zh: 彧聞聲歔欷，涕淚交下，梁武為之不樂。

translations.literal: Yu hearing the music sighed and wept, tears crossing — Wu of Liang for it was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sighed and wept at the music; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 自前後奔叛，皆候旨稱魏為偽，唯彧表啟常雲魏臨淮王。

translations.literal: Of those before and after who fled and rebelled, all waited on instruction to call Wei false — only Yu in memorials always said Prince of Linhuai of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Other defectors called Wei a false dynasty at court's cue; only Yu in his memorials still wrote Prince of Linhuai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 梁武體彧雅性，不以為責。

translations.literal: Wu of Liang honored Yu's refined nature and did not blame him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor respected Yu's refinement and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 及知莊帝踐阼，彧以母老請還，辭旨懇切。

translations.literal: When he learned Emperor Zhuangang had ascended the throne, Yu because his mother was old requested return — his words earnest and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Emperor Zhuangang had taken the throne, Yu begged to return because his mother was old; his plea was urgent and sharp.

sentences.zh: 梁武惜其人才，又難違其意，遣其僕射徐勉私勸彧留。

translations.literal: Wu of Liang prized his talent yet found it hard to go against his intention and sent his Vice Director Xu Mian privately to urge Yu to stay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized his talent but could not refuse his wish; he sent Vice Director Xu Mian privately to persuade him to stay.

sentences.zh: 彧曰：「死猶願北，況於生也？

translations.literal: Yu said: "In death I would still wish the north — how much more in life?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Even in death I would choose the north — how much more while I live?"

sentences.zh: 」梁武乃以禮遣。

translations.literal: Wu of Liang thereupon sent him off with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor then sent him home with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 彧性至孝。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was utmost filial.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 自經違離，不進酒肉；

translations.literal: From the time of separation he took no wine or meat;
translations.idiomatic: From the day he left his mother he took no wine or meat;

sentences.zh: 憔悴容貌，見者傷之。

translations.literal: His haggard countenance — those who saw him were wounded by it.
translations.idiomatic: his face grew haggard; all who saw him were moved.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書令、大司馬，兼錄尚書。

translations.literal: He held posts Minister Director of Affairs, Grand Marshal, concurrently Recorder of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister Director, Grand Marshal, and concurrent Recorder of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊帝追崇武宣王為文穆皇帝，廟號肅祖，母李妃為文穆皇后。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangang posthumously honored Martial Emperor Wu of Xuan as Cultured and Solemn Emperor, temple name Su Ancestor, mother Consort Li as Cultured and Solemn Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangang posthumously honored Martial Emperor Wu of Xuan as Cultured and Solemn Emperor, temple name Su Ancestor, and his mother Consort Li as Cultured and Solemn Empress.

sentences.zh: 將遷神主於太廟，以孝文為伯考。

translations.literal: When about to move the imperial tablets to the Ancestral Temple, making Emperor Xiaowen a father's younger brother in worship.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared to move their spirit tablets into the Ancestral Temple, it treated Emperor Xiaowen as a father's younger brother in the rites.

sentences.zh: 彧表諫，以為：「漢祖創業，香街有太上之廟；

translations.literal: Yu memorialized remonstrance, considering that: "Han founder created the enterprise — Xiang Street had the Grand Supreme's temple;
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated in a memorial: "When the Han founder began the enterprise, Xiang Street held the Grand Supreme's temple;

sentences.zh: 光武中興，南頓立春陵之寢。

translations.literal: Guangwu in the restoration — Nandun had established Chunling's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: when Guangwu restored the house, Nandun had Chunling's shrine.

sentences.zh: 元帝之于光武，疏為絕服，猶尚身奉子道，入繼大宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan to Emperor Guangwu was distant, severed mourning — yet still personally upheld the son's way, entering to succeed the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan to Guangwu was only a distant kinsman, past the mourning limit, yet still served him as a son and entered the great lineage.

sentences.zh: 高祖之于聖躬，親實猶子，陛下既纂洪緒，豈宜加伯考之名？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu to the sacred person was in kinship really like son — Your Majesty having already inherited the great succession, how can you add the father's younger brother's name?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu to Your Majesty's person was in truth like father to son; having inherited the great succession, how can you add a father's younger brother to the temple?

sentences.zh: 且漢宣之繼孝昭，斯乃上後叔祖，豈忘宗承考妣？

translations.literal: Moreover when Han Xuandi succeeded Emperor Xiaozhao, that was making a younger uncle the superior ancestor — how could he forget the lineage's receiving the father and mother in worship?
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xuandi succeeded Xiaozhao, he elevated a younger uncle — yet he did not forget the lineage that received father and mother in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 蓋以大義斯奪。

translations.literal: It was because the great principle was thus displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Great principle overrode kinship.

sentences.zh: 及金德將興，宣王受寄，景王意在毀冕，文王心規裂冠。

translations.literal: When Jin's Virtue was about to rise, Prince Xuan received commission, Prince Jing's intent lay in destroying the crown, Prince Wen's heart schemed splitting the cap.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's mandate rose, Prince Xuan took the regency; Prince Jing aimed to cast off the crown; Prince Wen plotted to split the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖祭則魏主，而權歸晉室。

translations.literal: Though in sacrifice it was still Wei as ruler, power returned to Jin's house.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice still named Wei, but power passed to Jin.

sentences.zh: 昆之與季，實傾曹氏。

translations.literal: Kun and Ji in fact overturned Cao's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Kun and Ji in fact overturned the Cao house.

sentences.zh: 且子元宣王塚胤，文王成其大業。

translations.literal: Moreover Ziyuan was Prince Xuan's tomb progeny, Prince Wen completed his great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan was Xuan's line from the tomb; Wen finished the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 故晉武繼文祖武，宣有伯考之稱。

translations.literal: Therefore Jin Wudi succeeded literary ancestor and martial ancestor — Xuan rightly had the father's younger brother's designation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jin Wudi succeeded the literary and martial ancestors; Xuan rightly bore the title of father's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 以今類古，恐或非儔。

translations.literal: Taking today as type of antiquity, I fear it may not be paired.
translations.idiomatic: To compare today with that past, I fear the cases do not match.

sentences.zh: 高祖德溢寰中，道超無外。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu — virtue overflowed within the seas, the Way surpassed beyond all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's virtue filled the realm; his Way surpassed all bounds.

sentences.zh: 肅祖雖勳格宇宙，猶曾奉贄稱臣。

translations.literal: Su Ancestor though merit reached the cosmos, still once offered tribute and called himself subject.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ancestor's merit spanned the cosmos, yet he had once offered tribute and called himself a subject.

sentences.zh: 穆後稟德坤元，復將配享乾位。

translations.literal: Empress Mu bearing virtue of Kun the earth, again will be paired to enjoy the Qian position.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mu embodied earth's virtue and was again to be paired with heaven in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 此乃君臣並筵，嫂叔同室，曆觀墳籍，未有其事。

translations.literal: This is ruler and subject sharing one mat, elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband in one chamber — scanning tomb records through the ages, there has not been this matter.
translations.idiomatic: That would seat ruler and subject at one table and brother's wife with husband's brother in one hall — in all the tombs and annals, nothing like it exists.

sentences.zh: 」時莊帝意銳，朝臣無敢言者，唯彧與吏部尚書李神俊並有表聞。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Zhuangang's intent was sharp, court ministers dared not speak — only Yu and Personnel Minister Li Shenjun both had memorials heard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangang's mind was set; no minister dared speak — only Yu and Personnel Minister Li Shenjun submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「文穆皇帝勳格四表，道邁百王，是用考循舊範，恭上尊號。

translations.literal: Edict reply said: "Cultured and Solemn Emperor's merit reached the four quarters, the Way surpassed the hundred kings, therefore we examine and follow the old pattern, respectfully raising the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "Cultured and Solemn Emperor's merit reached the four seas and his Way surpassed the hundred kings; we therefore follow old precedent and raise his honored title.

sentences.zh: 王表雲漢太上於香街，南頓於春陵。

translations.literal: The prince's memorial says Han set the Grand Supreme at Xiang Street, Nandun at Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial cites Han's Grand Supreme at Xiang Street and Nandun at Chunling.

sentences.zh: 漢高不因瓜瓞之緒，光武又無世及之德，皆身受符命，不由父祖。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu did not rely on melon-and-vine succession, Guangwu also had no virtue of generation upon generation — both personally received the mandate, not through fathers and grandfathers.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu did not inherit through collateral lines; Guangwu had no hereditary merit — both received the mandate themselves, not from forefathers.

sentences.zh: 別廟異寢，于理何差？

translations.literal: Separate temples and different shrines — in principle what difference?
translations.idiomatic: Separate temples and different shrines — what difference in principle?

sentences.zh: 文穆皇帝天眷人宅，歷數有歸。

translations.literal: Cultured and Solemn Emperor heaven's favor human dwelling, the sequence had its return.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured and Solemn Emperor had heaven's favor and the people's dwelling; the succession had its due return.

sentences.zh: 朕忝承下武，遂主神器。

translations.literal: We humbly inherit the lower martial, thereupon master the divine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly inherit the martial line and now hold the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 既帝業有統，漢氏非倫。

translations.literal: Since the imperial enterprise has its succession, Han's house is not the parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial line is continuous, the Han cases are not parallel.

sentences.zh: 若以昔況今，不當移寢。

translations.literal: If by past measuring present, one should not move the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: If the past governs the present, you say we should not move the shrine.

sentences.zh: 則魏太祖、晉景帝雖王跡已顯，皆以人臣而終，豈得與餘帝別廟，有闕餘序？

translations.literal: Then Wei Taizu and Jin Jingdi though kingly traces were already manifest, both ended as human subjects — how can they share separate temples with the rest of emperors, lacking in the remaining order?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei Taizu and Jin Jingdi, though their kingship was plain, died as subjects — can they have separate temples apart from other emperors and break the sequence?

sentences.zh: 漢郡國立廟者，欲尊高祖之德，使饗遍天下」非關太廟神主，獨在外祠薦。

translations.literal: Han commanderies and states establishing temples — desired to honor Gaozu's virtue, making offerings reach all under heaven" not concerning Ancestral Temple spirit tablets, alone in outer shrines offering.
translations.idiomatic: When Han commanderies and kingdoms built temples, it was to spread Gaozu's virtue through offerings everywhere — not the Ancestral Temple tablets kept in outer shrines.

sentences.zh: 漢宣之父，亦非勳德所出，雖不追尊，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: Han Xuan's father also was not from merit and virtue issuing forth — though not pursued in honor, is it not acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi's father likewise owed nothing to merit — though not ennobled posthumously, is that not acceptable?

sentences.zh: 伯考之名，自是尊卑之稱，何必准古而言非類也。

translations.literal: Father's younger brother's name is itself a title of honor and baseness — why must one follow antiquity and speak of non-kind?
translations.idiomatic: The title father's younger brother is itself a rank of seniority — why must antiquity forbid what fits?

sentences.zh: 復雲君臣同列，嫂叔共室。

translations.literal: Again saying ruler and subject in the same row, elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband sharing a chamber.
translations.idiomatic: You also object that ruler and subject would sit in one row and brother's wife with husband's brother in one chamber.

sentences.zh: 當以文穆皇帝昔遂臣道，以此為疑。

translations.literal: It should be because Cultured and Solemn Emperor in the past followed the subject's way — for this there is doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is because Cultured and Solemn Emperor once stood in the subject's place — hence your doubt.

sentences.zh: 《禮》'天子元子猶士'，禘祫豈不得同室乎？

translations.literal: The Rites 'the Son of Heaven's eldest son is still like a scholar' — di and fu sacrifices, how can they not share one chamber?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say the crown prince is still like a scholar — for di and fu sacrifices, may they not share one hall?

sentences.zh: 且晉文、景共為一代，議者雲世限七，主無定數。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin Wen and Jing together are one generation — debaters say the world limit is seven, the main without fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wen and Jing belong to one generation; some say the limit is seven generations, but the main line has no fixed count.

sentences.zh: 昭穆既同，明有共室之理。

translations.literal: Zhao and Mu being the same, clearly there is principle of sharing a chamber.
translations.idiomatic: If zhao and mu align, they clearly may share a chamber.

sentences.zh: 禮既有祔，嫂叔何嫌？

translations.literal: Rites already have fu — elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband, what scruple?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites already allow fu pairing — what scruple remains for brother's wife and husband's brother?

sentences.zh: 《禮》，大祖、禰一廟，豈無婦舅共室也？

translations.literal: The Rites, Great Ancestor and Father Ancestor one temple — how can there be no wife's uncle sharing a chamber?
translations.idiomatic: Great Ancestor and Father Ancestor share one temple in the Rites — may wife's uncle not share a hall?

sentences.zh: 若專以共室為疑，容可更議遷毀。

translations.literal: If solely taking sharing a chamber as doubt, perhaps one may again deliberate moving and destroying.
translations.idiomatic: If sharing a chamber alone is the objection, we may debate removal instead.

sentences.zh: 」莊帝既逼諸妹之請，此詞意黃門侍郎常景、中書侍郎邢子才所贊成也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangang already pressed by the younger sisters' request, this wording Yellow Gate Attendant Chang Jing and Secretariat Attendant Xing Zicai both approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangang, pressed by his younger sisters' plea, adopted language that Yellow Gate Attendant Chang Jing and Secretariat Attendant Xing Zicai had endorsed.

sentences.zh: 又追尊兄彭城王為孝宣帝。

translations.literal: Again posthumously honoring elder brother Prince of Pengcheng as Filial and Solemn Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also posthumously honored his elder brother Prince of Pengcheng as Filial and Solemn Emperor.

sentences.zh: 彧又面諫曰：「陛下作而不法，後世何觀？

translations.literal: Yu again remonstrated to his face, saying: "Your Majesty acts without following law — how will posterity view it?
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated again in person: "Your Majesty acts without precedent — what will posterity see?

sentences.zh: 曆尋書籍，未有其事。

translations.literal: Searching through books and records, there has not been this matter."
translations.idiomatic: Search the books — nothing like this exists."

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及神主入廟。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablets entered the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the tablets entered the temple,

sentences.zh: 復敕百官悉陪從，一依乘輿之式。

translations.literal: Again ordered all officials to accompany, entirely following the imperial carriage's form.
translations.idiomatic: he again ordered every official to attend, all in the form reserved for the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 彧上表以為：「爰自中古，迄于下葉，崇尚君親，褒明功懿，乃有皇號，終無帝名。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial considering: "From middle antiquity down to lower leaves, honoring ruler and kin, praising and clarifying merit and virtue — there were imperial titles, ultimately no emperor names.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized: "From middle antiquity to later ages, honoring rulers and kin and praising merit used imperial titles, never emperor names.

sentences.zh: 今若去帝，直留皇名，求之古義，少有依准。

translations.literal: Now if one removes emperor, leaving only imperial name, seeking it in ancient meaning, few have reliance.
translations.idiomatic: To drop emperor and keep only imperial title finds little support in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」又不納。

translations.literal: Again not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Again the court did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，除彧司徒公。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Yu was removed to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Yu was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃兆率眾奄至，出東掖門，為賊所獲。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao led the host suddenly arriving, exiting the eastern side gate, he was seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao's army suddenly arrived, Yu left by the eastern side gate and was seized.

sentences.zh: 見兆，辭色不屈，為群胡所毆，薨。

translations.literal: Seeing Zhao, his words and color did not bend; he was beaten by the Hu mob and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhao his speech and bearing did not break; the Hu mob beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝末，贈大將軍、太師、太尉公、錄尚書事，諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu he was posthumously given Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, Recorder of the Secretariat affairs, posthumous title Cultured and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Cultured and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 彧美風韻，善進止，衣冠之下，雅有容則。

translations.literal: Yu had beautiful bearing and wind, skilled in advancing and stopping — below cap and gown he had elegant rules of appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had fine presence and grace in movement; even in ordinary dress he kept an elegant bearing.

sentences.zh: 博覽群書，不為章句，所制文藻，雖多亡失，猶有傳於世者。

translations.literal: Broadly reading the many books, not making chapter-and-sentence commentary; the literary pieces he composed, though many are lost, still have some transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely without pedantic glossing; much of his writing is lost, but some still circulates.

sentences.zh: 然居官不能清白，所進舉止於親婭，為識者所譏。

translations.literal: Yet in office he could not be pure and white; what he advanced stopped at affinal kin — those with insight ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in office he was not clean-handed; his promotions favored in-laws, which the knowing mocked.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: Without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 弟孝友，少有時譽，襲爵臨淮王，累遷滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xiaoyou, in youth had reputation of the time, succeeded to Linhuai kingship, promoted in stages to Governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiaoyou, famed in youth, inherited Linhuai and rose to Governor of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政溫和，好行小惠，不能清白，而無所侵犯，百姓亦以此便之。

translations.literal: In government warm and mild, liking to practice small favors, could not be pure and white yet without encroachment — the common people also for this found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild and fond of small favors; he was not clean but did not prey on the people, who found him easy to live under.

sentences.zh: 魏靜帝宴齊文襄于華林園，孝友因醉自譽，又云：「陛下許賜臣能。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei banqueted Qi Wenxiang at Hualin Garden; Xiaoyou because of drunkenness praised himself, also saying: "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Qi Wenxiang at Hualin Garden; Xiaoyou, drunk, boasted and said, "Your Majesty promised to grant me talent."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「朕恆聞王自道清。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "We constantly hear the prince call himself pure."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "We always hear you call yourself incorrupt."

sentences.zh: 」文襄曰：「臨淮王雅旨舍罪。

translations.literal: Wenxiang said: "Prince of Linhuai in refined intent forgives offense."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Prince of Linhuai in his refinement pardons the slip."

sentences.zh: 」於是君臣俱笑而不罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers laughed and let it pass.

sentences.zh: 孝友明于政理，嘗奏表曰：

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was clear in government principle, once submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou understood governance and once submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 令制百家為黨族，二十家為閭，五家為比鄰。

translations.literal: Present regulations make a hundred households a party-clan, twenty households a lane, five households a neighboring unit.
translations.idiomatic: "Present law makes a hundred households a party, twenty a lane, five a neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 百家之內，有帥二十五，徵發皆免，苦樂不均。

translations.literal: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five leaders; levies and labor are all exempt for them — bitter and sweet not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Within each hundred households are twenty-five leaders exempt from levy and corvée — the burden falls unevenly.

sentences.zh: 羊少狼多，復有蠶食。

translations.literal: Sheep few, wolves many, again there is silkworm-devouring.
translations.idiomatic: Too few bear the load, too many feed on it; layer on layer they devour the people.

sentences.zh: 此之為弊久矣。

translations.literal: This as harm has been long.
translations.idiomatic: This abuse is old.

sentences.zh: 京邑諸坊，或七八百家，唯一里正、二史，庶事無闕，而況外州乎？

translations.literal: Capital wards — some seven or eight hundred households with only one lane chief and two clerks, miscellaneous affairs without lack — how much more the outer provinces?
translations.idiomatic: In the capital some wards have seven or eight hundred households yet only one lane chief and two clerks, and affairs still run — how much more in the provinces?

sentences.zh: 請依舊置，三正之名不改，而百家為於，四閭，閭二比，計族少十二丁，得十二匹貲絹。

translations.literal: Request according to old establishment, the three chiefs' names not changed, yet a hundred households as unit, four lanes, two neighborhoods per lane — calculating clans, twelve fewer ding, obtaining twelve bolts of silk tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old structure, keep the three chief titles, but make a hundred households the unit, four lanes, two neighborhoods per lane — twelve fewer adult males per clan, twelve bolts of silk tribute gained.

sentences.zh: 略計見管之戶，應二萬餘族，一歲出貲絹二十四萬匹。

translations.literal: Roughly calculating present registered households, should be more than twenty thousand clans — one year issuing twenty-four thousand bolts of silk tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly, registered households yield more than twenty thousand clans — twenty-four thousand bolts of silk a year.

sentences.zh: 十五丁出一番兵，計得一萬六千兵。

translations.literal: Fifteen ding produce one rotation soldier — calculating, obtaining sixteen thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen ding supply one rotating soldier — about sixteen thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 此富國安人之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way to enrich the state and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: That is the way to enrich the state and secure the people.

sentences.zh: 古諸侯娶九女，士有一妻二妾。

translations.literal: Ancient feudal lords took nine women, scholars had one wife and two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient feudal lords took nine wives; scholars had one wife and two concubines.

sentences.zh: 《晉令》：諸王置妾八人；

translations.literal: Jin regulations: all princes set eight concubines;
translations.idiomatic: Jin law allowed princes eight concubines;

sentences.zh: 郡君、侯，妾六人。

translations.literal: commandery lords and marquises, concubines six.
translations.idiomatic: commandery lords and marquises six.

sentences.zh: 《官品令》：第一、第二品有四妾；

translations.literal: Office Rank regulations: first and second rank have four concubines;
translations.idiomatic: Office Rank law gave first and second ranks four concubines;

sentences.zh: 第三、第四有三妾；

translations.literal: third and fourth have three concubines;
translations.idiomatic: third and fourth ranks three;

sentences.zh: 第五、第六有二妾；

translations.literal: fifth and sixth have two concubines;
translations.idiomatic: fifth and sixth two;

sentences.zh: 第七、第八有一妾。

translations.literal: seventh and eighth have one concubine.
translations.idiomatic: seventh and eighth one.

sentences.zh: 所以陰教聿修，繼祠有廣。

translations.literal: Therefore yin teaching is grandly cultivated, continuing sacrifice has breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the women's quarter was maintained and the sacrificial line broadened.

sentences.zh: 廣繼嗣，孝也。

translations.literal: Broadening continuing heirs is filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Many heirs are filial piety.

sentences.zh: 修陰教，禮也。

translations.literal: Cultivating yin teaching is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Maintaining the women's quarter is ritual.

sentences.zh: 而聖朝忽棄此數，由來漸久，將相多尚公主，王侯娶後族，故無妾媵，習以為常。

translations.literal: Yet the holy court suddenly abandoned these numbers — from coming it has been gradual and long; generals and ministers mostly esteem princesses, kings and marquises marry empresses' kin, therefore without concubine attendants, habit becomes constant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court has long abandoned these numbers; ministers marry imperial princesses, kings and marquises take empresses' kin — concubines vanished and custom froze.

sentences.zh: 婦人多幸，生逢今世，舉朝略是無妾，天下殆皆一妻。

translations.literal: Women mostly fortunate, born meeting this age — the whole court roughly without concubines, all under heaven nearly all one wife.
translations.idiomatic: Women are fortunate to live now: the court almost has no concubines; the realm is nearly all monogamous.

sentences.zh: 設令人強志廣娶，則家道離索，身事迍邅，內外親知共相嗤怪。

translations.literal: Suppose one forced will and broadly took wives — then family way scattered, personal affairs obstructed, inner and outer kin together would mock.
translations.idiomatic: If a man forced himself to take many wives, his household would fracture, his affairs stall, and kin and neighbors would laugh.

sentences.zh: 凡今之人，通無准節。

translations.literal: All people today universally lack standard and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Today everyone lacks a standard.

sentences.zh: 父母嫁女，則教之以妒；

translations.literal: Parents marrying daughters then teach them jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: Parents marrying daughters teach jealousy;

sentences.zh: 姑姊逢迎，必相勸以忌。

translations.literal: aunts and elder sisters in meeting and sending off must mutually urge scruple.
translations.idiomatic: aunts and sisters urge suspicion.

sentences.zh: 持制夫為婦德，以能妒為女工。

translations.literal: Holding control of the husband as wife's virtue, taking ability at jealousy as woman's work.
translations.idiomatic: Controlling the husband is called wifely virtue; skill in jealousy, woman's craft.

sentences.zh: 自雲受人欺，畏他笑我。

translations.literal: Self-saying receiving people's bullying, fearing others' laughing at oneself.
translations.idiomatic: They say they are bullied and fear being mocked.

sentences.zh: 王公猶自一心，以下何敢二意！

translations.literal: Kings and dukes still themselves one heart — how dare those below have two intents!
translations.idiomatic: Even kings and dukes keep one heart — how dare inferiors have two!

sentences.zh: 夫妒忌之心生，則妻妾之禮廢；

translations.literal: When jealousy's heart is born, then wife-and-concubine ritual is abolished;
translations.idiomatic: When jealousy rises, wife-and-concubine ritual dies;

sentences.zh: 妻妾之禮廢，則姦淫之兆興，斯臣之所以毒恨者也。

translations.literal: wife-and-concubine ritual abolished, then adultery's omen rises — this is why your subject bitterly hates it.
translations.idiomatic: when that ritual dies, adultery follows — this your subject bitterly hates.

sentences.zh: 請以王、公、第一品娶八，通妻以備九女；

translations.literal: Request with kings and dukes, first rank taking eight, common wife to complete nine women;
translations.idiomatic: Let kings, dukes, and first rank take eight concubines plus wife for nine women;

sentences.zh: 稱事二品備七；

translations.literal: according to office second rank completing seven;
translations.idiomatic: second rank seven;

sentences.zh: 三品、四品備五；

translations.literal: third and fourth rank completing five;
translations.idiomatic: third and fourth five;

sentences.zh: 五品、六品則一妻二妾。

translations.literal: fifth and sixth rank then one wife two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: fifth and sixth one wife and two concubines.

sentences.zh: 限以一周，悉令充數。

translations.literal: Limit to one cycle, all ordered to fill the number.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year all must fill their quota.

sentences.zh: 若不充數，及待妾非禮，使妻妒加捶撻，免所居官。

translations.literal: If not filling the number, and awaiting concubines not by ritual, making the wife jealous and adding beating — remove the office held.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever falls short, or keeps concubines irregularly, or lets a jealous wife beat them — strip his office.

sentences.zh: 其妻無子而不娶妾，斯則自絕，無以血食祖父，請科不孝之罪，離遣其妻。

translations.literal: If the wife has no sons and does not take concubines, this is self-cutting-off — no way to blood-offer to grandfathers, request sentencing the unfilial crime, divorce and send away the wife.
translations.idiomatic: A wife without sons who will not accept concubines cuts off the line — sentence unfilial conduct and divorce her.

sentences.zh: 臣之赤心，義唯家國，欲使吉凶無不合禮，貴賤各有其宜。

translations.literal: Your subject's red heart, righteousness solely for family and state, desires to make auspicious and inauspicious all not depart from ritual, noble and base each have their fit.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's sole aim is the family and state: let ritual govern fortune and misfortune, and each rank keep its place.

sentences.zh: 省人帥以出兵丁，立倉儲以豐穀食。

translations.literal: Reduce people-leading to send out military ding, establish granaries to enrich grain food.
translations.idiomatic: Cut petty chiefs to raise soldiers; build granaries to fill them.

sentences.zh: 設賞格以禽奸盜，行典令以示朝章。

translations.literal: Set reward grids to capture treachery and theft, enact canonical orders to display court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Set rewards to catch thieves; publish statutes to show the court's law.

sentences.zh: 庶使足食足兵，人信之矣。

translations.literal: May it make sufficient food and sufficient soldiers, people trust it.
translations.idiomatic: Then food and arms will suffice and the people will trust the throne.

sentences.zh: 又冒申妻妾之數，正欲使王侯將相，功臣子弟，苗胤滿朝，傳祚無窮，此臣之志也。

translations.literal: Again presumptuously declaring wives' and concubines' numbers — just desires to make kings, marquises, generals, ministers, meritorious ministers' sons and younger brothers, seed and lineage fill the court, transmission without end — this is your subject's aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: I also urge restoring concubine quotas so princes, ministers, and their sons may fill the court with heirs and the line never end — that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 詔付有司，議奏不同。

translations.literal: Edict handed to relevant offices, deliberation memorial different.
translations.idiomatic: The edict went to the ministries; their report disagreed.

sentences.zh: 孝友又言：「今人生為皁隸，葬擬王侯，存沒異途，無復節制。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou again said: "Now people alive as black slaves, burial imitating kings and marquises — alive and dead different paths, again without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou added: "Men live like bondsmen yet bury like princes — life and death follow different rules, and restraint is gone.

sentences.zh: 崇壯丘隴，盛飾祭儀，鄰里相榮，稱為至孝。

translations.literal: Honoring and magnifying mound and ridge, flourishing ornament of sacrifice ritual — neighbors mutually glorify, calling it utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: They raise great mounds and lavish funerals; neighbors praise it as perfect filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又夫婦之始，王化所先，共食合瓢，足以成禮。

translations.literal: Also husband-and-wife's beginning is kingly transformation's first — sharing food and joining gourds suffices to complete ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage is the start of royal teaching; shared food and joined gourds are ritual enough.

sentences.zh: 而今之富者彌奢，同牢之設，甚於祭槃。

translations.literal: Yet today's rich increasingly extravagant, same-cage setting surpasses sacrificial trays.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rich grow more extravagant; wedding feasts outdo sacrificial spreads.

sentences.zh: 累魚成山，山有林木，林木之上，鸞鳳斯存。

translations.literal: Piling fish into mountains, mountains have forest trees, above forest trees phoenixes and simurghs exist.
translations.idiomatic: They pile fish into mountains, set trees on them, and perch phoenixes atop —

sentences.zh: 徒有煩勞，終成委棄，仰惟天意，其或不然。

translations.literal: Only having troublesome labor, ultimately becoming abandoned cast-off — looking up to heaven's intent, perhaps it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: mere labor ending in waste. Heaven's intent, I think, is otherwise.

sentences.zh: 請自茲以後，若婚葬過禮者，以違旨論。

translations.literal: Request from now after, if marriage and burial exceed ritual, treat by violating the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whoever exceeds ritual in marriage or burial violates the edict.

sentences.zh: 官司不加糾劾，即與同罪。

translations.literal: If officials do not add investigation and impeachment, then same crime.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who fail to investigate share the guilt."

sentences.zh: 孝友在尹積年，以法自守，甚著聲稱。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou at the capital accumulated years, with law self-guarding, very marked in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou served many years as capital intendant, kept the law himself, and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 然性無骨鯁，善事權勢，為正直者所譏。

translations.literal: Yet his nature lacked backbone, good at serving power and influence — upright ones ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked backbone and courted the powerful; the upright mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，准例降爵，封臨淮縣公，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, according to precedent rank was lowered, enfeoffed Marquis of Linhuai county, appointed Honored Grandee of Light.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qi Tianbao his rank was reduced by precedent to Marquis of Linhuai county and Honored Grandee of Light.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，被詔入晉陽宮，出與元暉業同被害。

translations.literal: Second year winter, ordered into Jinyang Palace, went out and with Yuan Huiye was together harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second winter he was summoned to Jinyang Palace and killed together with Yuan Huiye.

sentences.zh: 昌弟孚，字秀和，少有令譽。

translations.literal: Younger brother of the clan Fu, courtesy name Xiuhe, in youth had fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman younger brother Fu, courtesy Xiuhe, was famed in youth.

sentences.zh: 侍中游肇、并州刺史高聰、司徒崔光等見孚，咸曰：「此子當准的人物，恨吾徒衰暮，不及見耳。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary You Zhao, Governor of Bingzhou Gao Cong, Minister Cui Guang and others seeing Fu all said: "This child should match the great men of the age — pity our company is aged and declining, not reaching to see."
translations.idiomatic: You Zhao, Gao Cong of Bingzhou, Cui Guang, and others said of him: "This boy will match the great men of the age — pity we are old and will not see it."

sentences.zh: 」累遷兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Promoted in stages to concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，宦者幹政，孚乃總括古今名妃賢後，凡為四卷，奏之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling at court, eunuchs interfering in government — Fu thereupon summarized through the ages famous consorts and worthy queens, altogether four scrolls, submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling ruled and eunuchs meddled, Fu compiled four scrolls of famous consorts and worthy empresses and presented them.

sentences.zh: 遷左丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瑰既得反國，其人大饑，相率入塞，阿那瑰上表請台振給。

translations.literal: Rouran lord Anagui having regained his state, his people greatly starved, together entering the passes — Anagui submitted a memorial requesting court relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran lord Anagui recovered his realm his people starved and poured through the passes; Anagui asked the court for relief.

sentences.zh: 詔孚為北道行台，詣彼振恤，孚陳便宜表曰：

translations.literal: Edict made Fu Northern Route Commissioner, going there to relieve and comfort; Fu submitted a convenient-terms memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The court made Fu Northern Route Commissioner to bring aid; he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 皮服之人，未嘗粒食，宜從俗因利，拯其所無。

translations.literal: Leather-clothed people have never grain-eaten — should follow custom and take advantage, saving what they lack.
translations.idiomatic: "Leather-clad peoples have never lived on grain; aid should follow their ways and supply what they lack.

sentences.zh: 昔漢建武中，單于款塞，時轉河東米Я二萬五千斛、牛羊三萬六千頭以給之。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han Jianwu, the Shanyu submitted to the passes — at the time transferred Hedong rice twenty-five thousand hu, cattle and sheep thirty-six thousand head to give them.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Jianwu, when the Shanyu came to the frontier, the court sent twenty-five thousand hu of Hedong grain and thirty-six thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 斯則前代和戎，撫新柔遠之長策也。

translations.literal: This then is former age harmonizing with the Rong, comforting the new and softening the distant — the long strategy.
translations.idiomatic: That was the old policy of pacifying the Rong and winning the newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 乞以牸牛產羊，糊其口食。

translations.literal: Beg to use breeding cows producing sheep, paste their mouth food.
translations.idiomatic: Grant breeding cattle and ewes and feed them dairy.

sentences.zh: 且畜牧繁息，是其所便；

translations.literal: Moreover animal husbandry multiplying is what they are skilled at;
translations.idiomatic: Herding is their strength;

sentences.zh: 毛血之利，惠兼衣食。

translations.literal: fur and blood's profit, favor joining clothes and food.
translations.idiomatic: wool and meat serve both clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 又尚書奏云：如其仍住七州，隨寬置之。

translations.literal: Also the Secretariat memorial said: if they still dwell in the seven provinces, broadly place them as width allows.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat also proposed settling them across seven provinces wherever space allowed.

sentences.zh: 臣謂人情戀本，寧肯徙內？

translations.literal: Your subject considers human feeling clings to roots — would they willingly move inward?
translations.idiomatic: I say people cling to home — will they willingly move inland?

sentences.zh: 若依臣請，給振雜畜，愛本重鄉，必還舊土。

translations.literal: If following your subject's request, giving relief mixed livestock, loving roots and honoring native place, they will surely return to old lands.
translations.idiomatic: If you follow my plan and give mixed herds, cherishing home, they will return to their old lands.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，禁留益損。

translations.literal: If not so, forbidding and detaining increases harm.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise detention only deepens the harm.

sentences.zh: 假令逼徙，事非久計。

translations.literal: Suppose forced migration — the affair is not a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Forced migration is no long-term policy.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 人面獸心，去留難測。

translations.literal: Human face, beast heart — going and staying hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Human faces hide beast hearts; loyalty is hard to read.

sentences.zh: 既易水草，屙恙將多；

translations.literal: Having changed water and grass, illness and harm will be many;
translations.idiomatic: Change their pasture and sickness multiplies;

sentences.zh: 憂愁致困，死亡必甚。

translations.literal: worry and distress leading to exhaustion, death will be very severe.
translations.idiomatic: grief and want will kill many.

sentences.zh: 兼其餘類，尚在沙磧；

translations.literal: Moreover the rest of their kind still are in sand and gravel;
translations.idiomatic: Their kin remain in the desert;

sentences.zh: 脫出狂勃，翻歸舊巢，必殘掠邑裏，遺毒百姓。

translations.literal: if they escape wild rage and turn back to old nests, they will surely ravage districts and towns, leaving poison to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: if they break free and return, they will ravage the border and poison the people.

sentences.zh: 亂而方塞，未若杜其未萌。

translations.literal: Chaos and then blocking the passes — not as good as stopping it before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: To seal the passes after chaos is worse than stopping the sprout.

sentences.zh: 又貿遷起於上古，交易行於中世。

translations.literal: Also trade and transport rose in high antiquity, exchange proceeded in middle ages.
translations.idiomatic: Trade is ancient; barter flourished in middle antiquity.

sentences.zh: 漢與胡通，亦立關市。

translations.literal: Han with Hu connected, also established pass markets.
translations.idiomatic: Han dealt with the Hu and set border markets.

sentences.zh: 今北人阻饑，命懸溝壑；

translations.literal: Now northerners obstructed by famine, life suspended over ditch and ravine;
translations.idiomatic: Now the north starves; lives hang over the abyss.

sentences.zh: 公給之外，必求市易。

translations.literal: beyond public giving, they must seek market exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond public relief they must trade.

sentences.zh: 彼若願求，宜見聽許。

translations.literal: If they wish to request, it is fitting to be heard and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If they ask to buy, grant it.

sentences.zh: 又云：

translations.literal: Also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote:

sentences.zh: 營大者不計小名，圖遠者弗拘近利。

translations.literal: Managing great affairs does not calculate small names, plotting distant does not bind near profit.
translations.idiomatic: "Great undertakings ignore petty reputation; distant plans do not cling to immediate gain.

sentences.zh: 雖戎狄衰盛，歷代不同，叛服之情，略可論討。

translations.literal: Though Rong and Di decline and flourish differ by generation, the feeling of rebellion and submission can roughly be discussed and examined.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian strength shifts with each age, but their pattern of submission and revolt can be weighed.

sentences.zh: 周之北伐，僅獲中規；

translations.literal: Zhou's northern campaign barely obtained middle regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's northern campaigns barely achieved middling success;

sentences.zh: 漢氏外攘，裁收下策。

translations.literal: Han House's outer expansion only barely took the lower strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Han outward expansion often took the lesser plan.

sentences.zh: 昔在代京，恆為重備，將帥勞止，甲士疲力。

translations.literal: Formerly at Dai capital, constantly was heavy defense — generals and commanders labor stopped, armored soldiers strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the old capital Dai the frontier was always heavily garrisoned; generals wore out and soldiers drained away.

sentences.zh: 計前世苦之，力未能致。

translations.literal: Considering former generations suffered it, strength could not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Past dynasties suffered this because force alone could not finish the work.

sentences.zh: 今天祚大魏，亂亡在彼。

translations.literal: Today heaven's mandate is great Wei, chaos and ruin are over there.
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven favors great Wei; their disorder is their own.

sentences.zh: 朝廷垂天覆之恩，廓大造之德，鳩其散亡，禮送令反，宜因此時，善思遠策。

translations.literal: Court droops heaven-covering favor, broadly great-making virtue, gathering their scattered and lost, rite sending ordering return — should at this time well think distant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The court spreads sheltering grace and vast mercy, gathers their scattered, and sends them home with ritual — this is the moment for far-sighted policy.

sentences.zh: 竊以理雖萬變，可以一觀；

translations.literal: Your subject considers principle though ten thousand changes, can be viewed in one observation;
translations.idiomatic: Principle shifts in ten thousand ways yet may be read in one glance;

sentences.zh: 來事雖懸，易以往卜。

translations.literal: coming affairs though suspended, easy to use past to divine.
translations.idiomatic: the future, though uncertain, may be divined from the past.

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣之世，呼韓款塞，漢遣董忠、韓昌領邊郡士馬，送出朔方，因留衛助。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han Xuan's age, Huhanye submitted to the passes — Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang leading border commandery soldiers and horses, escorting out beyond Shuofang, thereupon remaining to guard and assist.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Xuandi's time Huhanye came to the passes; Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang with border troops to escort him beyond Shuofang and left guards to assist.

sentences.zh: 又光武時，亦令中郎將段彬置安集掾史，隨單于所在，參察動靜。

translations.literal: Also in Guangwu's time, again ordered Central Gentlemen Duan Bin to set Pacification clerks, following the Shanyu's place, examining movement and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu, Central Gentlemen Duan Bin placed Pacification clerks with the Shanyu to watch his movements.

sentences.zh: 斯皆守吉之元龜，安邊之勝策。

translations.literal: These all are guarding the auspicious's primary tortoise, settling the border's winning strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Those were the tortoise of good fortune and the winning border strategy.

sentences.zh: 計今朝廷成功，不減曩時，蠕蠕國弊，亦同疇日。

translations.literal: Considering today's court's achievement, not reduced from former times; Rouran state's exhaustion, also the same as yesterday.
translations.idiomatic: Today's court is no weaker than those ages; Rouran's exhaustion matches yesterday's.

sentences.zh: 宜准昔成謀，略依舊事，借其所閑地，聽使田牧。

translations.literal: Should follow former completed plans, roughly follow old affairs, borrowing their idle lands, hearing them field and pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the old completed plans: lend idle land and let them herd.

sentences.zh: 粗置官屬，示相慰撫。

translations.literal: Roughly set official subordinates, displaying mutual comfort and soothing.
translations.idiomatic: Place officials to show care.

sentences.zh: 嚴戒邊兵，以見保衛。

translations.literal: Strictly warn border soldiers, to display protection and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Warn the border troops to protect them visibly.

sentences.zh: 馭以仁寬，縻以久策。

translations.literal: Driving with benevolence and breadth, tethering with long policy.
translations.idiomatic: Rule them with kindness and bind them with long policy.

sentences.zh: 使親不至矯詐，疏不容叛反。

translations.literal: Making close not reach deceit, distant not tolerate rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the near from deceit and the far from revolt.

sentences.zh: 今北鎮諸將，舊常雲一人代外邏，因令防察。

translations.literal: Now Northern Garrison generals, old constant saying one man replaces outer rotation, thereupon ordered defense and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Garrison generals still rotate one officer to the frontier for inspection.

sentences.zh: 所謂天子有道，守在四夷者也。

translations.literal: This is called the Son of Heaven has the Way, defense kept in the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: That is what it means to say: when the Son of Heaven holds the Way, defense lies in the four barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又云：

translations.literal: Also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote:

sentences.zh: 先人有奪人之心，待降如受強敵。

translations.literal: Forefathers had heart of seizing others' — treating submission like receiving a strong enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "Forefathers kept the heart of conquest even toward those who submitted.

sentences.zh: 武非尋外，亦以防內。

translations.literal: Martial not only seeking outer, also to guard inner.
translations.idiomatic: Arms serve not only the frontier but the interior.

sentences.zh: 若從處分割配，諸州鎮遼遠，非轉輸可到，悔叛之情，變起難測。

translations.literal: If following placement division and assignment to the various provinces and garrisons, distant and far, not transport and delivery can reach — repentant rebellion's feeling, change arising hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: If we split and assign them among distant provinces, supply cannot follow and repentant revolt may arise unmeasured.

sentences.zh: 又居人畜業，布在原野，戎夷性貪，見則思盜；

translations.literal: Also dwelling people raising livestock, cloth spread on original wilds — Rong and Yi nature greedy, seeing then thinking theft;
translations.idiomatic: Their herds lie open on the steppe; barbarians are greedy and theft tempts them;

sentences.zh: 防彼肅此，少兵不堪。

translations.literal: guarding them strict here, few soldiers cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: guarding one place leaves too few men elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 渾流之際，易相干犯。

translations.literal: At confused currents' juncture, easy mutually to violate.
translations.idiomatic: In turbulent times clashes come easily.

sentences.zh: 驅之還本，未必樂去，配州內徙，復不肯從。

translations.literal: Driving them back to roots, not necessarily pleased to go; assigning within provinces inner move, again not willing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Drive them home and they may not wish to go; move them inland and they will refuse.

sentences.zh: 既其如此，為費必大。

translations.literal: Since it is thus, expense must be great.
translations.idiomatic: Either way the cost will be vast.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許。

translations.literal: Court did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not accept.

sentences.zh: 孚持白武幡勞阿那瑰于柔玄、懷荒二鎮間。

translations.literal: Fu held white martial banner consoling Anagui between Rouxuan and Huaihuang two garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Fu carried the white peace banner to console Anagui between Rouxuan and Huaihuang.

sentences.zh: 阿那環瑰眾號三十萬，陰有異意，遂拘留孚。

translations.literal: Anagui's host numbered three hundred thousand, secretly had different intent, thereupon detained Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui's following was said to number three hundred thousand; he secretly harbored other plans and detained Fu.

sentences.zh: 載以韞車，日給酪一升、肉一段。

translations.literal: Loaded in covered cart, daily given one sheng of curdled milk, one section of meat.
translations.idiomatic: They loaded him in a covered cart and gave him daily a sheng of curd and a portion of meat.

sentences.zh: 每集其眾，坐孚車廂，稱為行台，甚加禮敬。

translations.literal: Each gathering his host, seating Fu in the carriage compartment, calling him Route Commissioner, greatly adding ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he assembled his men he seated Fu in the carriage compartment, called him Route Commissioner, and treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 阿那瑰遂南過，至舊京。

translations.literal: Anagui thereupon passed south, reaching old capital.
translations.idiomatic: Anagui then marched south to the old capital.

sentences.zh: 後遣孚等還，因上表謝罪。

translations.literal: Later sent Fu and others back, thereupon submitted memorial apologizing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent Fu and the others back and submitted an apology.

sentences.zh: 有司以孚事下廷尉，丞高謙之雲孚辱命，處孚流罪。

translations.literal: Relevant offices because of Fu's affair handed down to Court of Justice, Vice Director Gao Qianzhi saying Fu disgraced the mandate, sentenced Fu to exile crime.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries referred Fu to the Court of Justice; Vice Director Gao Qianzhi said Fu had disgraced his commission and urged exile.

sentences.zh: 後拜冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Later appointed Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 孚勸課農桑，境內稱慈父，鄰州號曰神君。

translations.literal: Fu urged mulberry and farming lessons, within the borders called kind father, neighboring provinces titled divine lord.
translations.idiomatic: Fu promoted sericulture and farming; his province called him kind father, neighboring ones divine lord.

sentences.zh: 先是，州人張孟都、張洪建、馬潘、崔獨憐、張叔緒、崔醜、張天宜、崔思哲等八人，皆屯保林野，不臣王命，州郡號曰八王。

translations.literal: Earlier, provincials Zhang Mengdu, Zhang Hongjian, Ma Pan, Cui Dulian, Zhang Shuxu, Cui Chou, Zhang Tianyi, Cui Sizhe and eight others — all garrisoned fortresses in forest wilds, not serving the king's command, provinces and commanderies called them Eight Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Eight men of the province — Zhang Mengdu, Zhang Hongjian, Ma Pan, Cui Dulian, Zhang Shuxu, Cui Chou, Zhang Tianyi, and Cui Sizhe — had held wild fortresses and defied the throne; the region called them the Eight Kings.

sentences.zh: 孚至，皆請入城，願致死效力。

translations.literal: When Fu arrived, all requested entering the cities, willing to die to offer strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu arrived they all entered the cities and offered their lives in service.

sentences.zh: 後為葛榮所陷，為榮所執。

translations.literal: Later was trapped by Ge Rong, seized by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ge Rong captured him.

sentences.zh: 兄祐為防城都督，兄子禮為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Elder brother You was Defense City Metropolitan Commander, elder brother's son Li was Recording Office Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His brother You was Defense City Metropolitan Commander; his nephew Li was Recording Office Attendant.

sentences.zh: 榮欲先害子禮，孚請先死以贖子禮，叩頭流血，榮乃舍之。

translations.literal: Rong wished first to harm son Li — Fu requested first death to redeem son Li, knocking head blood flowing, Rong thereupon spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong meant to kill Li first; Fu begged to die in his stead, knocking his head until blood ran, and Rong spared Li.

sentences.zh: 又大集將士，議其死事。

translations.literal: Again greatly gathering generals and soldiers, deliberating his death affair.
translations.idiomatic: Rong again gathered his officers to decide Fu's fate.

sentences.zh: 孚兄弟各誣己引過，爭相為死。

translations.literal: Fu's brothers each falsely accused themselves drawing fault, competing to be the one to die.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's brothers each claimed the fault as his own and vied to die.

sentences.zh: 又孟都、潘紹等數百人皆叩頭就法，請活使君。

translations.literal: Also Mengdu, Pan Shao and several hundred men all knocked heads approaching execution, requesting to spare the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Mengdu, Pan Shao, and hundreds more bowed their heads for execution, begging Rong to spare their lord.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「此魏之誠臣義士也。

translations.literal: Rong said: "These are Wei's sincere subjects and righteous knights."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "These are Wei's loyal and righteous men."

sentences.zh: 」凡同禁五百人，皆得免。

translations.literal: Altogether those together imprisoned five hundred men, all obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred held with him were all released.

sentences.zh: 榮卒，還除冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Rong died, returned and removed to Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death he returned as Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，授孚東道行台、彭城郡王。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, invested Fu Eastern Route Commissioner, Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he made Fu Eastern Route Commissioner and Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 孚封顥逆書送朝廷，天子嘉之。

translations.literal: Fu sealed Hao's rebellious letter and sent to court — the Son of Heaven praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu sealed Hao's rebel letters and sent them to court; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 顥卒，封孚萬年鄉男。

translations.literal: When Hao died, enfeoffed Fu Marquis of Wannian township.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao died, Fu was enfeoffed Marquis of Wannian township.

sentences.zh: 永安末，樂器殘缺，莊帝命孚監儀注。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an, musical instruments incomplete — Emperor Zhuangang ordered Fu to supervise ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yong'an the ritual instruments were broken; Emperor Zhuangang ordered Fu to supervise the regulations.

sentences.zh: 孚上表曰：

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized:

sentences.zh: 昔太和中，中書監高閭、太樂令公孫崇修造金石，數十年間，乃奏成功。

translations.literal: Formerly in great harmony, Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu, Grand Music Master Gongsun Chong repaired and made metal and stone — several decades between, then memorialized completion.
translations.idiomatic: "In the great Taihe era, Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu and Grand Music Master Gongsun Chong rebuilt the bells and stones; decades passed before they reported success.

sentences.zh: 時大集儒生，考其得失。

translations.literal: At the time greatly gathered Confucian scholars, examining their gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars were gathered to judge the result.

sentences.zh: 太常卿劉芳請別營造，久而方就。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Ritual Liu Fang requested separate construction — long afterward then completed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Liu Fang asked for a separate set; long after, that too was finished.

sentences.zh: 復召公卿量校合否，論者沸騰，莫有適從。

translations.literal: Again summoned dukes and ministers to measure and collate whether fitting, debaters boiling, none having what to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and ministers were summoned to compare them; debate boiled and no consensus held.

sentences.zh: 登被旨敕，並見施用。

translations.literal: Deng received imperial edict and command, all seen applied.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen ordered both adopted.

sentences.zh: 往歲大軍入洛，戎馬交馳，所有樂器，亡失垂盡。

translations.literal: Past year great army entered Luoyang, war horses crossing — all musical instruments, lost almost completely.
