translations.idiomatic: Last year the great army entered Luoyang; in the fighting nearly all instruments were lost.

sentences.zh: 臣至太樂署，問太樂令張乾龜等，雲承前以來，置宮懸四箱，栒虡六架，東北架編黃鐘之磬十四。

translations.literal: Your subject reaching Grand Music Office, asked Grand Music Master Zhang Qian'gui and others, saying from former coming down, set palace suspension four cases, wooden tiger six frames, northeast frame compiled Yellow Bell's chime fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Music Office, Grand Music Master Zhang Qian'gui told me that since former times the court kept four cases of palace bells, six wooden frames, and on the northeast frame fourteen Yellow Bell chimes.

sentences.zh: 雖器名黃鐘，而聲實夷則；

translations.literal: Though the instrument's name Yellow Bell, the sound in fact Yize;
translations.idiomatic: Though named Yellow Bell, they actually sound Yize;

sentences.zh: 考之音制，不甚諧韻。

translations.literal: Examining sound regulation, not very harmonious in rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: and measured against the pitch standard they are badly out of tune.

sentences.zh: 姑洗懸于東北，太蔟編於西北，蕤賓列於西南。

translations.literal: Gu Xian hung in the northeast, Tai Cu arrayed in the northwest, Rui Bin ranged in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xian hung in the northeast, Tai Cu in the northwest, Rui Bin in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 並皆器象差位，調律不和。

translations.literal: All alike were vessels and images in wrong positions, tuning and pitch not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Every instrument stood in the wrong place; pitch and tuning did not agree.

sentences.zh: 又有儀鐘十四，虡懸架首，初不叩擊，今便刪廢，以從正則。

translations.literal: There were also fourteen ceremonial bells, frames with heads of beasts, at first not struck; now let them be abolished to follow the correct rule.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen ceremonial bells on beast-headed frames had never been struck; he now proposed abolishing them to restore proper order.

sentences.zh: 臣今據《周禮鳧氏》修廣之規，《磬氏》倨句之法，吹律求聲，叩鐘求音；

translations.literal: Your servant now according to the Zhou Rite's Bell-Maker's broad rules and the Stone-Chime-Maker's obtuse-acute method, blows pitch pipes to seek tones, strikes bells to seek sound;
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Zhou Rite's Bell-Maker for dimensions and the Stone-Chime-Maker for angles, blowing pipes to fix pitch and striking bells to test tone.

sentences.zh: 損除繁雜，討論實錄。

translations.literal: Cut away the redundant, discuss what is solid and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped away excess and settled on what the records actually required.

sentences.zh: 依十二月為十二宮。

translations.literal: According to the twelve months as twelve palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He aligned the twelve months with twelve palace stations.

sentences.zh: 各准辰次，當位懸設。

translations.literal: Each matched the chronogram position and was hung in its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Each matched its season and hung where it belonged.

sentences.zh: 月聲既備，隨用擊奏。

translations.literal: When the monthly tones were complete, they were struck as needed in performance.
translations.idiomatic: Once every month's tone was in place, musicians could strike them as the rite demanded.

sentences.zh: 則會還相為宮之義，又得律呂相生之體。

translations.literal: Then was obtained the meaning of mutual circulation among palaces, and also the substance of pitch-generating one another.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the bells could cycle through the modes and embody the law by which pitches beget one another.

sentences.zh: 今量鐘磬之數，各以十二架為定。

translations.literal: Now measuring the numbers of bells and chimes, each was fixed at twelve frames.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the count of bells and stone chimes at twelve frames each.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 于時搢紳之士，咸往觀聽，靡不咨嗟歎服而反。

translations.literal: At that time gentry and officials all went to watch and listen; none failed to sigh in admiration and return.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen flocked to hear the new arrangement and left sighing in admiration.

sentences.zh: 太傅、錄尚書長孫承業妙解聲律，特復稱善。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor and Director of the Masters of Writing Changsun Chengye was skilled in pitch and excellently praised it again.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Changsun Chengye, a master of pitch, praised the reform again.

sentences.zh: 復從孝武帝入關，除尚書左僕射、扶風郡王。

translations.literal: Again followed Emperor Xiaowu into the pass, made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu west, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and was enfeoffed Prince of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 尋監國史。

translations.literal: Soon supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised the national history.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、兼尚書令、太保。

translations.literal: In succession held posts Minister of Works, concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Minister of Works, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕主與孚相識，先請見孚，然後遣女。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran ruler knew Fu well and first asked to see Fu, then sent his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan knew Fu and insisted on seeing him before sending his daughter.

sentences.zh: 於是乃使孚行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent Fu on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore sent Fu on the embassy.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕君臣見孚，莫不歡悅，奉皇后來歸。

translations.literal: Rouran lord and ministers seeing Fu were all delighted and escorted the empress back in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran lord and ministers rejoiced at Fu and escorted their queen into Wei marriage.

sentences.zh: 孚性機辯，好酒，貌短而禿。

translations.literal: Fu by nature was quick-witted, loved wine, short in appearance and bald.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was quick-witted, fond of wine, short, and bald.

sentences.zh: 周文帝偏所眷顧，嘗於室內置酒十瓨，瓨餘一斛，上皆加帽，欲戲孚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou especially favored him; once in the chamber he set out ten jars of wine, each jar holding more than a bushel, all capped, wishing to tease Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou favored him; once he set ten capped jars in the room, each holding over a bushel, to tease him.

sentences.zh: 孚適入室，見即驚喜，曰：「吾兄弟輩甚無禮，何為竊入王家，匡坐相對？

translations.literal: Fu just entering the room, seeing them at once was startled and pleased, saying: "Our brothers are very rude—why break into the royal house and sit facing one another?
translations.idiomatic: Fu entered, feigned shock and delight, and said, "Brothers, how rude—why break into the royal house and sit drinking together?

sentences.zh: 宜早還宅也。

translations.literal: You should return home early."
translations.idiomatic: Go home at once."

sentences.zh: 」因持酒歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the wine and left.
translations.idiomatic: He carried off the wine.

sentences.zh: 周文撫手大笑。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen clapped his hands and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen clapped and laughed.

sentences.zh: 後遇風患，手足不隨，口不能言，乃左手畫地作字，乞解所任。

translations.literal: Later he met wind illness; hands and feet did not follow; mouth could not speak; then with the left hand he drew on the ground characters, begging release from his posts.
translations.idiomatic: Later wind illness left him mute and paralyzed; he wrote on the floor with his left hand, begging to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 三奏不許。

translations.literal: Three memorials were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Three memorials were refused.

sentences.zh: 遷太傅。

translations.literal: Transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: Died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 帝親臨，百官赴吊。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person; the hundred officials went to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person; officials attended the mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈大司馬、錄尚書事，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously Grand Marshal and Director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Grand Marshal and director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 子端嗣，位大行台尚書、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Son Duan inherited, post Grand Marshalate Director of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan inherited, becoming director on the grand marshalate staff and inspector of Hua.

sentences.zh: 性疏佷，頗以基地驕物，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: By nature coarse and obstinate, he rather looked down on others from his base lands; opinion of the time despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Coarse and proud of his estates, he looked down on others; men of the day despised him.

sentences.zh: 石侯弟嘉，少沉敏，喜慍不形於色，兼有武略。

translations.literal: Younger brother of the Stone Marquis, Jia, young was deep and keen, joy and anger did not show on the face, and also had military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, younger brother of the Stone Marquis, was grave and keen from youth; joy and anger never showed, and he had military talent.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，拜徐州刺史，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen he was made Inspector of Xuzhou, very authoritative and gracious.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowen's accession he became inspector of Xuzhou, stern yet merciful.

sentences.zh: 後封廣陽王，以紹建後。

translations.literal: Later enfeoffed Prince of Guangyang to continue the founding line.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangyang to continue the founding house.

sentences.zh: 孝文南伐，詔嘉斷均口。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen campaigned south he ordered Jia to cut off Junkou.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiaowen's southern campaign he ordered Jia to seal Junkou.

sentences.zh: 嘉違失指授，令賊得免。

translations.literal: Jia missed the command and let the bandits escape.
translations.idiomatic: Jia missed his orders and let the enemy escape.

sentences.zh: 帝怒責之曰：「叔祖定非世孫，何太不上類也！

translations.literal: The emperor angrily reproached him saying: "Uncle-grandsire surely is not a true descendant—how unlike your kind!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Uncle, you cannot be a true heir of the house—how unlike your line!"

sentences.zh: 」及將大漸，遺詔以嘉為尚書左僕射，與咸陽王禧等輔政。

translations.literal: When about to die he left in the testamentary edict that Jia be Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others to assist government.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he named Jia left vice director, with Prince Xi of Xianyang and others as regents.

sentences.zh: 遷司州牧。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia became governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉表請於京四面築坊三百二十，各周一千二百步，乞發三正復丁，以充茲役。

translations.literal: Jia memorialized asking to build three hundred twenty wards around the capital on four sides, each circuiting twelve hundred paces, begging to levy the three categories of corvée and exempted households to fill this labor.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to ring the capital with three hundred twenty wards of twelve hundred paces each, levying every corvée category to build them.

sentences.zh: 雖有暫勞，奸盜永止。

translations.literal: Though there was temporary toil, treachery and theft would forever cease.
translations.idiomatic: The labor would be brief, he said, but theft would end for good.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 拜衛大將軍、尚書令，除儀同三司。

translations.literal: Made Guards General, Director of the Masters of Writing, given equal thirds with the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He became guards general and director of the Masters of Writing with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 嘉后妃宜都王穆壽孫女，司空從妹也。

translations.literal: Jia's consort was granddaughter of Prince Yidu Mu Shou, younger cousin of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was granddaughter of Prince Yidu Mu Shou and cousin to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 聰明婦人。

translations.literal: An intelligent woman.
translations.idiomatic: She was a clever woman.

sentences.zh: 及為嘉妃，多所匡贊，光益家道。

translations.literal: When she became Jia's consort she often corrected and aided, brightening the household way.
translations.idiomatic: As Jia's princess she often guided him and brought honor to the house.

sentences.zh: 子深，字知遠，襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Shen, style Zhiyuan, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen, style Zhiyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 孝明初，拜肆州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming he was made Inspector of Si.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaoming's accession he became inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 預行恩信，胡人便之，劫盜止息。

translations.literal: He beforehand practiced grace and trust; the Hu people found it convenient; robbery and banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with grace beforehand; the Hu were content and banditry stopped.

sentences.zh: 後為恆州刺史，在州多所受納，政以賄成。

translations.literal: Later became Inspector of Heng, in the province much accepting bribes, government accomplished by gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Later as inspector of Heng he took endless bribes; office ran on graft.

sentences.zh: 私家有馬千匹者，必取百匹，以此為恆。

translations.literal: If a household had a thousand horses he surely took a hundred; this he made constant.
translations.idiomatic: Households with a thousand horses owed him a hundred by custom.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中尚書，未拜。

translations.literal: In succession promoted Palace Director of the Masters of Writing, not yet invested.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted palace director but never received investiture.

sentences.zh: 坐淫城陽王徽妃於氏，為徽表訟。

translations.literal: For lying with Prince of Chengyang Hui's consort Lady Yu he was sued by Hui in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He lay with Prince Hui of Chengyang's consort Lady Yu; Hui sued him.

sentences.zh: 詔付丞相、高陽王雍等宗室議決其罪，以王還第。

translations.literal: An edict handed him to the Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong and other clansmen to decide his crime; he was sent back to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The edict sent him to Prince Yong of Gaoyang and kinsmen for judgment; he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 及沃野鎮人破六韓拔陵反叛，臨淮王彧討之失利，詔深為北道大都督，受尚書令李崇節度。

translations.literal: When the people of Woye garrison Po-lu-ling Pa-ling rebelled, Prince of Huaiyang Yu campaigning against them failed; an edict made Shen Grand Commander of the Northern Route, receiving the direction of Director Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Woye rose under Pa-ling, Prince Yu of Huaiyang failed; Shen was named northern commander under Director Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 時東道都督崔暹敗于白道，深等諸軍退還朔州。

translations.literal: At that time eastern-route commander Cui Xian was defeated at White Way; Shen and the armies retreated to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern commander Cui Xian lost at White Way; Shen's armies fell back to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 深上書曰：

translations.literal: Shen submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shen memorialized:

sentences.zh: 邊豎構逆，以成紛梗，其所由來，非一朝也。

translations.literal: Frontier rebels have raised trouble and made disorder; their origin is not of a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: "Border rebels did not arise in a day.

sentences.zh: 昔皇始以移防為重，盛簡親賢，擁麾作鎮，配以高門子弟，以死防遏。

translations.literal: Formerly in Huangshi the shift of garrisons was treated as weighty; they chose kin and worthies, gave banners as commanders, paired them with sons of great houses to die holding the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangshi's day garrison duty was sacred: kinsmen and worthies commanded the passes, noble sons sent to die on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 不但不廢仕宦，至乃偏得復除。

translations.literal: Not only was office not abolished—for them even exemptions were granted in full.
translations.idiomatic: They kept office and full tax exemptions.

sentences.zh: 當時人物，忻慕為之。

translations.literal: Men of that time admired and yearned for it.
translations.idiomatic: Men envied the posting.

sentences.zh: 及太和在曆。

translations.literal: When the Taihe reign began.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taihe era began,

sentences.zh: 僕射李沖當官任事，涼州土人，悉免廝役；

translations.literal: Vice Director Li Chong held office and managed affairs; Liangzhou natives were all freed from corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Chong freed Liangzhou natives from corvée

sentences.zh: 豐沛舊門，仍防邊戍。

translations.literal: Feng and Pei old clans still guarded the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: while Feng and Pei clans still garrisoned the border.

sentences.zh: 自非得罪當世，莫肯與之為伍。

translations.literal: Unless guilty in their generation none would join them.
translations.idiomatic: None but the disgraced would serve with them.

sentences.zh: 征鎮驅使為虞候、白直，一生推遷，不過軍主。

translations.literal: Campaign garrisons were driven as scouts and runners; a lifetime of promotion did not pass company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison soldiers became scouts and runners; a lifetime might end as company commander.

sentences.zh: 然其往世房分，留居京者，得上品通官；

translations.literal: Yet their former household branches remaining in the capital could obtain upper-grade regular office;
translations.idiomatic: Kin who stayed in the capital won high office;

sentences.zh: 在鎮者，便為清途所隔。

translations.literal: those at the garrisons were cut off from the clear path.
translations.idiomatic: those at the posts were barred from promotion.

sentences.zh: 或投彼有北，以禦魑魅，多復逃胡鄉。

translations.literal: Some fled north to escape demons; many again fled into Hu districts.
translations.idiomatic: Some fled north or into Hu lands.

sentences.zh: 乃峻邊兵之格，鎮人浮游在外，皆聽流兵捉之。

translations.literal: Then they stiffened the rules on frontier soldiers; garrison men drifting outside were all heard as deserters to be seized by roaming patrols.
translations.idiomatic: Rules tightened; any garrison man abroad was treated as a deserter and seized.

sentences.zh: 於是少年不得從師，長者不得游宦。

translations.literal: Thus youths could not follow teachers, elders could not seek office.
translations.idiomatic: Youths could not study; elders could not seek office.

sentences.zh: 獨為匪人，言者流涕。

translations.literal: Alone made outlaws—those who spoke wept.
translations.idiomatic: They became outcasts, and men wept to speak of it.

sentences.zh: 自定鼎伊洛，邊任益輕，唯底滯凡才，出為鎮將。

translations.literal: From fixing the tripod at Yi and Luo the frontier post grew ever lighter; only the dullest talents went out as garrison generals.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, frontier command grew contemptible; only mediocrities were sent as generals.

sentences.zh: 轉相模習，專事聚斂。

translations.literal: Turning to imitate one another they specialized in amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: They copied one another and specialized in plunder.

sentences.zh: 或有諸方奸吏，犯罪配邊，為之指蹤，過弄官府；

translations.literal: Some were wicked officials from other regions, punished and sent to the frontier, who pointed the way and played with the government offices;
translations.idiomatic: Criminal officials banished to the frontier taught them how to squeeze the government;

sentences.zh: 政以賄立，莫能自改。

translations.literal: government stood on bribes and none could reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: rule ran on bribes, and none reformed.

sentences.zh: 咸言奸吏為此，無不切齒增怒。

translations.literal: All said wicked officials did this—none failed to gnash teeth in added rage.
translations.idiomatic: All blamed such officials and gnashed their teeth.

sentences.zh: 及阿那瑰背恩，縱掠竊奔，命師追之。

translations.literal: When Anagui turned traitor and let his plunderers flee, troops were ordered to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui betrayed the court and fled, the court sent an army in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 十五萬眾度沙漠，不日而還。

translations.literal: A hundred fifty thousand men crossed the desert and returned within days.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred fifty thousand crossed the desert and were home again within days.

sentences.zh: 邊人見此援師，便自意輕中國。

translations.literal: Frontier men seeing this relief army at once took China lightly in their own minds.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier men saw that army and despised the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 尚書令臣崇時即申聞，求改鎮為州，將允其願，抑亦先覺。

translations.literal: Director Li Chong at once reported, asking to change garrisons into provinces; the wish would have been granted—he also foresaw.
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Chong then asked to turn garrisons into provinces; the court would have agreed, and he foresaw the danger.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未許。

translations.literal: The court did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 而高闕戍主，率下失和，拔陵殺之為逆命；

translations.literal: Then the Gaogue garrison commander lost harmony below; Pa-ling killed him in rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: A Gaogue commander lost his men; Pa-ling killed him and rebelled;

sentences.zh: 攻城掠地，所見必誅。

translations.literal: besieging cities and seizing land, all he saw he put to death.
translations.idiomatic: wherever he marched he slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 王師屢北，賊党日盛。

translations.literal: Imperial armies repeatedly retreated north; rebel bands daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial armies retreated again and again while rebels swelled.

sentences.zh: 此段之舉，指望銷平。

translations.literal: This campaign was hoped to extinguish and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign was meant to crush them.

sentences.zh: 其崔暹雙輪不反，臣崇與臣，逡巡復路。

translations.literal: Yet Cui Xian's twin wheels did not return; Chong and your servant hesitated on the road back.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Cui Xian never returned; Chong and I limped back.

sentences.zh: 今者相與，還次雲中。

translations.literal: Now we together have halted again at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: We halt again at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 馬首是瞻，未便西邁。

translations.literal: Where the horses' heads look we have not yet turned west.
translations.idiomatic: The army will not yet march west.

sentences.zh: 將士之情，莫不解體。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers in spirit all lost bone.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' hearts are broken.

sentences.zh: 今日所慮，非止西北，將恐諸鎮尋亦如此。

translations.literal: Today's worry is not only the northwest; I fear every garrison will soon be the same.
translations.idiomatic: The peril is not only the northwest; every garrison may follow.

sentences.zh: 天下之事何易可量！

translations.literal: Affairs under heaven—how easily can they be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Who can measure what comes next under heaven?

sentences.zh: 時不納其策。

translations.literal: At the time they did not adopt his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 東西部敕勒之叛，朝議更思深言。

translations.literal: When the eastern and western tribes of the Tiele rebelled, court discussion again recalled Shen's words.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern and western Tiele rebelled, the court remembered Shen's warning.

sentences.zh: 遣兼黃門侍郎酈道元為大使，欲復鎮為州，以順人望。

translations.literal: They sent Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant Li Daoyuan as grand envoy, wishing again to change garrisons to provinces to follow popular hope.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Li Daoyuan as envoy to turn garrisons into provinces and appease the frontier.

sentences.zh: 會六鎮盡叛，不得施行。

translations.literal: But all six garrisons rebelled; it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All six garrisons rose before he could act.

sentences.zh: 深後上言：「今六鎮俱叛，二部高車亦同惡黨，以疲兵討之，必不制敵。

translations.literal: Shen later submitted saying: "Now all six garrisons rebel; the two divisions of Gaoche also share their evil party—with weary troops to attack them surely cannot control the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen wrote again: "All six garrisons rebel and both Gaoche divisions join them; weary troops cannot win.

sentences.zh: 請簡選兵，或留守恆州要處。

translations.literal: I beg to select troops, or hold the vital point at Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Choose fresh troops or hold Heng's key passes

sentences.zh: 更為後圖。」

translations.literal: Make plans again later."
translations.idiomatic: and plan again when the moment comes."

sentences.zh: 及李崇征還，深專總戎政。

translations.literal: When Li Chong returned from campaign, Shen alone held military government.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong returned, Shen alone held military authority.

sentences.zh: 拔陵避蠕蠕，南移度河。

translations.literal: Pa-ling avoided the Rouran and moved south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Pa-ling evaded the Rouran and crossed the river south.

sentences.zh: 先是，別將李叔仁以拔陵來逼，請求迎援，深赴之，前後降附二十萬人。

translations.literal: Earlier separate general Li Shuren because Pa-ling pressed asked for relief; Shen went to him; before and after two hundred thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Shuren had begged relief when Pa-ling pressed him; Shen marched to him and two hundred thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 深與行台元纂表求恆州北別立郡縣，安置降戶，隨宜振賚，息其亂心。

translations.literal: Shen with the Mobile Office Yuan Zuan memorialized asking north of Heng to separately establish commanderies and counties to settle the surrendered households, according to need to relieve and grant, quieting their rebellious hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Yuan Zuan of the mobile office asked to settle the surrendered north of Heng in new counties, feeding them to quiet rebellion.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: Not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 詔遣黃門侍郎楊置分散之于冀、定、瀛三州就食。

translations.literal: An edict sent Yellow Gate Attendant Yang to disperse them among Ji, Ding, and Ying three provinces for food.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Yang to scatter them among Ji, Ding, and Ying for grain.

sentences.zh: 深謂纂曰：「此輩復為乞活矣。

translations.literal: Shen said to Zuan: "These people again become beggars for life.
translations.idiomatic: Shen told Zuan, "You have made beggars of them again.

sentences.zh: 禍亂當由此作。」

translations.literal: Disaster and disorder will arise from this."
translations.idiomatic: Disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 既而鮮于修禮叛於定州，杜洛周反于幽州，其餘降戶，猶在恆州，遂欲推深為主。

translations.literal: Soon Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Dingzhou, Du Luozhou at Youzhou; the rest of the surrendered still at Heng then wished to make Shen their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Ding, Du Luozhou at You; the remaining surrendered at Heng tried to make Shen their chief.

sentences.zh: 深乃上書乞還京師。

translations.literal: Shen then submitted a memorial begging return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shen memorialized begging to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 令左衛將軍楊津代深為都督，以深為侍中、右衛將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Ordered Left Guards General Yang Jin to replace Shen as commander; Shen made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Right Guards General, Inspector of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Left guards general Yang Jin replaced him; Shen became attendant-in-ordinary, right guards general, and inspector of Ding.

sentences.zh: 時中山太守趙叔隆、別駕崔融討賊失利，台使劉審考核未訖，會賊逼中山，深乃令叔隆防境。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongshan Administrator Zhao Shulong and Vice Director Cui Rong attacking bandits failed; the office envoy Liu Shen was examining and not finished when bandits pressed Zhongshan; Shen then ordered Shulong to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Shulong and Cui Rong failed against rebels and inspector Liu Shen had not finished his review, bandits pressed Zhongshan; Shen ordered Shulong to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 審馳驛還京，雲深擅相放縱。

translations.literal: Shen galloped post-horses back to the capital, saying Shen on his own authority had been lax.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen raced to the capital accusing Guangyang Shen of lax command.

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽與深有隙，因此構之。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Hui and Shen had a rift; therefore he framed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Chengyang hated Shen and framed him.

sentences.zh: 乃征深為吏部尚書、兼中領軍。

translations.literal: Then summoned Shen as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrent Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was recalled as director of personnel and central army commander.

sentences.zh: 及深至都，明帝不欲使徽、深相憾，敕因宴會，令相和解。

translations.literal: When Shen reached the capital Emperor Ming did not wish Hui and Shen to resent each other; he ordered at a banquet that they reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Emperor Ming ordered a banquet to reconcile Shen and Hui.

sentences.zh: 徽銜不已。

translations.literal: Hui harbored resentment without end.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's grudge never ended.

sentences.zh: 後河間王琛等為鮮于修禮所敗，乃除深儀同三司、大都督。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Hejian Chen and others were defeated by Xianyu Xiuli; then Shen was made equal thirds with the Three Excellencies and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chen of Hejian fell to Xianyu Xiuli, Shen was made grand commander with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 章武王融為左都督，裴衍為右都督，並受深節度。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Rong was left commander, Pei Yan right commander, both receiving Shen's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong of Zhangwu commanded the left, Pei Yan the right, both under Shen.

sentences.zh: 徽因奏靈太后構深曰：「廣陽以愛子握兵在外，不可測也。

translations.literal: Hui therefore memorialized to Empress Dowager Ling framing Shen saying: "Guangyang holds his beloved son with troops outside—he cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Hui told Empress Ling, "Guangyang keeps his beloved son in command abroad—who can trust him?"

sentences.zh: 」乃敕章武王等潛相防備。

translations.literal: Then ordered Prince of Zhangwu and others secretly to guard against one another.
translations.idiomatic: She secretly ordered Rong and the others to watch him.

sentences.zh: 融遂以敕示深。

translations.literal: Rong then showed the edict to Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Rong showed Shen the edict.

sentences.zh: 深懼，事無大小，不敢自決。

translations.literal: Shen feared; on matters large and small he dared not decide himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shen grew afraid and dared decide nothing alone.

sentences.zh: 靈太后聞之，乃使問深意狀，乃具言曰：

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling hearing this sent to ask Shen's true intent; he then fully stated saying:
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked his mind; he answered at length:

sentences.zh: 往者元叉執權，移天徙日，而徽托附，無翼而飛。

translations.literal: Formerly when Yuan Cha held power he moved heaven and shifted the sun, yet Hui clung to him and flew without wings.
translations.idiomatic: "When Yuan Cha moved heaven and earth, Hui clung to him and rose without wings.

sentences.zh: 今大明反政，任寄唯重，以徽褊心，銜臣次骨。

translations.literal: Now the great brightness has returned to government; trust and commission are only weighty; because Hui's heart is narrow he hates your servant to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne is restored, yet Hui's narrow heart hates me to the bone.

sentences.zh: 臣以疏滯，遠離京輦，被其構阻，無所不為。

translations.literal: Your servant because coarse and stagnant was far from the capital carriage, framed and obstructed by him—there was nothing he did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Far from court, I was framed at every turn.

sentences.zh: 然臣昔不在其後，自此以來，翻成陵谷。

translations.literal: Yet your servant was not formerly behind him; from then until now it has turned into deep valley.
translations.idiomatic: I was never his follower; since then he has buried me.

sentences.zh: 徽遂一歲八遷，位居宰相；

translations.literal: Hui then eight promotions in one year, position reaching chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Hui was promoted eight times in a year to chancellor;

sentences.zh: 臣乃積年淹滯，有功不錄。

translations.literal: your servant was stalled many years, merit unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: I stagnated for years while merit went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 自徽執政以來，非但抑臣而已，北征之勳，皆被擁塞。

translations.literal: From when Hui held government, not only was your servant suppressed—northern expedition merits were all blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Since he took power he has blocked not only me but every northern merit.

sentences.zh: 將士告捷，終無片賞；

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers reporting victory in the end had not a shred of reward;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who won received nothing;

sentences.zh: 雖為表請，多不蒙遂。

translations.literal: though memorialized, many were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: memorials for reward were refused.

sentences.zh: 前留元摽據乎盛樂，後被重圍，析骸易子，倒懸一隅。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuan Biao was left at Shengle, later besieged in heavy rings; splitting bones they traded sons, hung upside down in a corner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Biao held Shengle until besieged; men ate their children; the city hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 嬰城二載，賊散之後，依階乞官，徽乃盤退，不允所請。

translations.literal: Besieged two years; after the bandits scattered, according to rank he begged office; Hui then turned back and did not grant what was asked.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he begged office by rank; Hui refused.

sentences.zh: 而徐州下邳戍主賈勳，法僧叛後，暫被圍逼，固守之勳，比之未重，乃立得州，即授開國。

translations.literal: Yet Xuzhou Xiapi garrison commander Jia Xun, after Faseng's rebellion was for a time besieged—the merit of firm defense compared with that was not heavier—yet he at once received a province and was enfeoffed a state founder.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xun held Xiapi through Faseng's siege with lesser merit yet won a province and a founding marquisate.

sentences.zh: 天下之事，其流一也，功同賞異，不平謂何！

translations.literal: Affairs under heaven flow one way—equal merit yet different reward; what is imbalance called!
translations.idiomatic: Merit is equal, reward unequal—what justice is that?

sentences.zh: 又驃騎李崇北征之日，啟募八州之人，聽用關西之格。

translations.literal: Also when Cavalry General Li Chong on the northern expedition opened recruitment of men from eight provinces, hearing use of the Guanxi scale.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong marched north he promised Guanxi pay to recruits from eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 及臣在後，依此科賞。

translations.literal: When your servant was behind, according to this rule he rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Behind him I paid by that scale.

sentences.zh: 復言北道征者，不得同于關西。

translations.literal: Again saying northern-route campaigners could not be the same as Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then said northern troops must not match Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 定襄陵廟之至重，平城守國之要鎮，若計此而論功，亦何負于秦楚？

translations.literal: Dingxiang tomb-shrine is of the utmost weight, Pingcheng guarding the state's vital fortress—if counting this to discuss merit, how is it inferior to Qin and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang's tombs and Pingcheng's walls weigh as heavy as Qin and Chu—how are their defenders less deserving?

sentences.zh: 但以嫉臣之故，便欲望風排抑。

translations.literal: Only because of hatred of your servant he then wished to suppress on sight of wind.
translations.idiomatic: He suppresses them only because they follow me.

sentences.zh: 然其當途以來，何直退勳而已。

translations.literal: Yet from when he held the road until now, how is it only retreating merit!
translations.idiomatic: His spite does not stop at denying merit.

sentences.zh: 但是隨臣征者，即便為所嫉。

translations.literal: Whoever followed your servant on campaign at once became what he envied.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who marched with me becomes his enemy.

sentences.zh: 統軍袁叔和曾經省訴，徽初言有理，又聞北征隸臣為統，應時變色。

translations.literal: Commander Yuan Shuhe once appealed to the ministry; Hui at first said there was reason, then hearing northern expedition was subordinate to your servant as commander, at once changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yuan Shuhe appealed; Hui first agreed, then turned hostile when he learned Shuhe served under me.

sentences.zh: 復令臣兄子仲顯異端訟臣，緝緝翩翩，謀相誹謗。

translations.literal: Again ordering your servant's brother's son Zhongxian to sue your servant with strange pleas, weaving and fluttering, plotting mutual slander.
translations.idiomatic: He set my nephew Zhongxian to sue me with endless slander.

sentences.zh: 言臣惡者，接以恩顏；

translations.literal: Those who spoke your servant's evil he met with favoring countenance;
translations.idiomatic: He smiles on those who call me wicked;

sentences.zh: 稱臣善者，即被嫌責。

translations.literal: those who called your servant good at once were suspected and reproached.
translations.idiomatic: he punishes those who praise me.

sentences.zh: 甄琛曾理臣屈，乃視之若仇讎；

translations.literal: Zhen Chen once judged your servant's wrong and then looked on him as enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen once judged my case fairly and became his foe;

sentences.zh: 徐紇頗言臣短，即待之如親戚。

translations.literal: Xu He often spoke your servant's faults yet was treated like a kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He spoke my faults yet is treated like kin.

sentences.zh: 又驃騎長史祖瑩，昔在軍中，妄增首級；

translations.literal: Also Cavalry General Chief Clerk Zu Ying, formerly in the army falsely added head-count;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ying, chief clerk to the cavalry general, once inflated head counts in camp;

sentences.zh: 矯亂戎行，蠹害軍府，獲罪有司，避命山澤。

translations.literal: distorting the army's march, harming the military office, guilty before the law, avoiding fate in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: he corrupted the army, fled justice to the hills,

sentences.zh: 直以謗臣之故，徽乃還雪其罪。

translations.literal: Only because of slandering your servant Hui then returned and cleared his crime.
translations.idiomatic: yet Hui cleared him because he slandered me.

sentences.zh: 臣府司馬劉敬，比送降人，既到定州，翻然背叛，賊如決河，豈其能擁。

translations.literal: Your servant's office Marshal Liu Jing, comparing in escorting surrendered men, when they reached Dingzhou turned and rebelled; bandits like a bursting river—how could he embrace them?
translations.idiomatic: My marshal Liu Jing escorted surrendered men who rebelled at Ding like a bursting river—how could he hold them?

sentences.zh: 且以臣府參僚，不免身首異處。

translations.literal: And because he was your servant's office staff, he did not escape body and head in different places.
translations.idiomatic: Because he served my office, he died dismembered.

sentences.zh: 徽既怒遷，舍其元惡，及胥徒。

translations.literal: Hui being angry and transferred, he let go the chief evil and grasped the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Hui punished clerks and spared the chief culprit.

sentences.zh: 從臣行者，莫不悚懼。

translations.literal: Those who followed your servant—none failed to tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: All who followed me tremble.

sentences.zh: 頃恆州之人，乞臣為刺史，徽乃斐然言不可測。

translations.literal: Recently the people of Heng begged your servant as inspector; Hui then spoke fluently that it could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng begged me as inspector, Hui called me unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 及降戶結謀，臣頻表啟，徽乃因執言此事。

translations.literal: When the surrendered plotted, your servant repeatedly memorialized; Hui then seized on this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrendered plotted, I reported it; he seized the tale.

sentences.zh: 及向定州，遠彼奸惡，又復論臣將有異志。

translations.literal: And when going to Dingzhou, far from those wicked men, again he spoke that your servant would have a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: As I went to Ding he again said I meant treason.

sentences.zh: 翻覆如此，欲相陷沒。

translations.literal: Turning over like this, wishing to trap and destroy.
translations.idiomatic: He twists every way to destroy me.

sentences.zh: 致令國朝，遽賜遷代。

translations.literal: Causing the dynastic court hastily to grant transfer and replacement.
translations.idiomatic: The court hurried my recall.

sentences.zh: 賊起之由，誰使然也？

translations.literal: The origin of the bandits' rise—who made it so?
translations.idiomatic: Who made the rebels rise?

sentences.zh: 徽既優幸，任隆一世，慕勢之徒，于臣何有！

translations.literal: Hui being favored and privileged, his commission lofty for a generation—those who admired power, what did they have toward your servant!
translations.idiomatic: Hui is favored for a generation; who courts power visits him, not me.

sentences.zh: 是故餘人攝選，車馬填門。

translations.literal: Therefore others when holding selection, carriages and horses filled the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When others held appointments, their gates choked with carriages.

sentences.zh: 及臣居邊，賓遊罕至。

translations.literal: When your servant dwelt on the frontier, guests and travelers rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier my gate was empty.

sentences.zh: 臣近比為慮其為梗，是以孜孜乞赴京闕。

translations.literal: Your servant recently feared he would be an obstruction, therefore diligently begged to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I begged the capital fearing he would block me.

sentences.zh: 屬流人舉斧，元戎垂翅，復從後命，自安無所；

translations.literal: Just when exiles raised axes and the grand commander drooped wings, again following the later order, self at ease nowhere;
translations.idiomatic: When exiles took up axes and armies folded, I obeyed again with nowhere to rest;

sentences.zh: 僶俛先驅，不敢辭事。

translations.literal: bowing head as vanguard, not daring to decline affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I bowed and marched ahead, not daring refuse.

sentences.zh: 及臣出都，行塵未滅，已聞在後，復生異議。

translations.literal: When your servant left the capital the marching dust was not yet settled when already heard behind of fresh different discussion.
translations.idiomatic: I had barely left the capital when fresh slander followed.

sentences.zh: 言臣將兒自隨，證為可疑之兆。

translations.literal: Saying your servant would have his son follow himself, proof of a suspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: He said I brought my son as proof of treason.

sentences.zh: 忽稱此以構亂。

translations.literal: Suddenly using this to frame disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He used that to cry rebellion.

sentences.zh: 悠悠之人，復傳音響，言左軍臣融、右軍臣衍皆受密敕，伺察臣事。

translations.literal: Loose people again transmitted sounds, saying left army your servant Rong, right army your servant Yan both received secret edicts to watch your servant's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors said Rong on the left and Yan on the right held secret orders to spy on me.

sentences.zh: 徽既用心如此，臣將何以自安？

translations.literal: Hui having used his heart thus, how can your servant secure himself?
translations.idiomatic: With Hui's heart thus, how can I be safe?

sentences.zh: 竊以天步未夷，國難猶梗；

translations.literal: I venture that the heavenly step is not yet level, national difficulty still blocks;
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet at peace; calamity still blocks the way.

sentences.zh: 方伯之任，於斯為急。

translations.literal: the duty of regional lords is at this time urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial command is urgent now.

sentences.zh: 徽昔臨籓，乃有人譽，及居端右，無聞焉爾。

translations.literal: Hui formerly on the frontier had men's praise; dwelling at the summit right, none heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was praised on the frontier; at court center he is unheard of.

sentences.zh: 今求出之為州，使得申其利用。

translations.literal: Now beg to send him out as a province, let him declare his useful service.
translations.idiomatic: Send him out to a province where he may prove useful.

sentences.zh: 徽若外從所長，臣無內慮之切。

translations.literal: If Hui outside follows his strength, your servant has no inner worry's cut.
translations.idiomatic: If he serves abroad by his talent, I need not fear him within.

sentences.zh: 脫蒙，公私幸甚。

translations.literal: If I receive this, public and private are greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Grant this and public and private alike will prosper."

sentences.zh: 深以兵士頻經退散，人無鬥情，連營轉柵，日行十里。

translations.literal: Shen because the soldiers had repeatedly retreated and scattered, men had no fighting heart; linking camps and turning palisades, each day marched ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's men had retreated so often they would not fight; he chained camps and crept ten li a day.

sentences.zh: 行達交津，隔水而陣。

translations.literal: March reaching Jiaojin, across water they formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaojin he drew up across the water.

sentences.zh: 賊修禮常與葛榮謀，後稍信朔州人毛普賢，榮常銜之。

translations.literal: Bandit Xiuli often plotted with Ge Rong; later he slightly trusted Shuozhou man Mao Puxian; Rong often resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuli often plotted with Ge Rong but later trusted Mao Puxian of Shuozhou, whom Rong resented.

sentences.zh: 普賢昔為深統軍，及在交津，深傳入諭之，普賢乃有降意。

translations.literal: Puxian formerly was Shen's commander; when at Jiaojin, Shen sent word urging him; Puxian then had intent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Puxian had served under Shen; at Jiaojin Shen urged him and he wavered toward surrender.

sentences.zh: 又使錄事參軍元晏說賊程殺鬼。

translations.literal: Also sent Recorder-Adjutant Yuan Yan to persuade bandit Cheng Shagui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yuan Yan to sway the bandit Cheng Shagui.

sentences.zh: 果相猜貳。

translations.literal: Indeed they mutually suspected and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion split the rebels.

sentences.zh: 葛榮遂殺普賢、修禮而自立。

translations.literal: Ge Rong then killed Puxian and Xiuli and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong killed Puxian and Xiuli and took command.

sentences.zh: 榮以新得大眾，上下未安，遂北度瀛州。

translations.literal: Rong because he newly had a great multitude, above and below not yet at peace, then went north crossing Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, uneasy with his new horde, marched north into Ying.

sentences.zh: 深便率眾北轉。

translations.literal: Shen then led the multitude turning north.
translations.idiomatic: Shen turned north after him.

sentences.zh: 榮東攻章武王融，融戰敗于白牛還。

translations.literal: Rong east attacked Prince of Zhangwu Rong; Rong was defeated at White Ox Return.
translations.idiomatic: Rong struck Prince Rong of Zhangwu and broke him at White Ox Return.

sentences.zh: 深遂退走，趣定州。

translations.literal: Shen then retreated running, hurrying to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fled toward Ding.

sentences.zh: 聞刺史楊津疑其有異志，乃止于州南佛寺。

translations.literal: Hearing Inspector Yang Jin suspected he had a different intent, he then stopped at a Buddhist temple south of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Inspector Yang Jin suspected treason, he halted at a temple south of the city.

sentences.zh: 停二日夜，乃召都督毛諡等六七人，臂肩為約，危難之際，期相拯恤。

translations.literal: Stopped two days and nights, then summoned Commanders Mao Mi and six or seven others, arms on shoulders as covenant, in peril's moment expecting to save and comfort one another.
translations.idiomatic: After two nights he arm-linked Mao Mi and six officers, swearing to save one another in peril.

sentences.zh: 諡疑深意異，乃密告津，雲深謀不軌。

translations.literal: Mi suspected Shen's intent was different and secretly reported to Jin, saying Shen plotted not to follow the law.
translations.idiomatic: Mi doubted him and told Jin that Shen plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 津遣諡討深。

translations.literal: Jin sent Mi to attack Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Mi against him.

sentences.zh: 深走出，諡叫噪追躡。

translations.literal: Shen ran out; Mi shouted and chased close.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fled; Mi shouted and pursued.

sentences.zh: 深與左右行至博陵郡界，逢賊遊騎，乃引詣葛榮。

translations.literal: Shen with attendants reaching Boling commandery border met bandit roaming horsemen, then led to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At Boling he met rebel scouts and was brought to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 賊徒見深，頗有喜者。

translations.literal: Bandit followers seeing Shen were somewhat pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Many rebels rejoiced to see him.

sentences.zh: 榮新自立，內惡之，乃害深。

translations.literal: Rong newly established himself, inwardly hated him, then harmed Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, newly risen, hated him inwardly and killed him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝追復王爵，贈司徒公，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang posthumously restored the princely title, posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang restored his princely rank, posthumously made him Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 湛弟瑾，尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Jin, Director of the Masters of Writing in the Sacrifices Section.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Jin was director of sacrifices in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後謀殺齊文襄。

translations.literal: Later plotted to kill Qi Emperor Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted to kill Emperor Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 事泄，合門伏法。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; the whole household suffered execution by law.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed; the whole clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 湛子法輪，紫光所生也。

translations.literal: Zhan's son Falun was born to Ziguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's son Falun was born to Lady Ziguang.

sentences.zh: 齊王矜湛覆滅，乃啟原之，復其爵土。

translations.literal: The Qi king pitied Zhan's extinction and then memorialized to restore him, restoring his title and lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor pitied Zhan's fall and restored Falun's title and lands.

sentences.zh: 南安王餘，真君三年封吳王，後改封南安王。

translations.literal: Prince of Nan'an Yu, in Zhenjun year three enfeoffed Prince of Wu, later changed to Prince of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed Prince of Wu in Zhenjun year three, later Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 太武暴崩，中常侍宗愛矯皇太后令迎立之，然後發喪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu suddenly collapsed, Palace Attendant Zong Ai forged the empress dowager's order to welcome and establish him, then afterward issued mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu died suddenly, Zong Ai forged the empress dowager's order, enthroned Yu, then announced mourning.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改年為永平。

translations.literal: Great amnesty, changed the era to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He declared a great amnesty and the era Yongping.

sentences.zh: 餘自以非次而立，厚遺群下，取悅於眾。

translations.literal: Yu himself because he was established out of order, richly gifted the ranks below, taking pleasure from the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his accession irregular, Yu lavished gifts on the court to win favor.

sentences.zh: 為長夜之飲，聲樂不絕。

translations.literal: Made long-night drinking; music and sound unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He held endless night feasts; music never stopped.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，帑藏空罄。

translations.literal: Within a ten-day month the treasury was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the treasury was bare.

sentences.zh: 尤好弋獵，出入無度。

translations.literal: He especially loved falconry and hunting, going out without measure.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 邊方告難，餘不恤之，百姓憤惋，而余晏如也。

translations.literal: The frontier reported hardship; Yu did not pity it; the hundred surnames were angry and grieved, yet Yu was serene.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier cried for help; Yu ignored it; the people raged while he remained serene.

sentences.zh: 宗愛權恣日甚，內外憚之。

translations.literal: Zong Ai's power grew daily; inside and outside feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ai's power grew daily; court and realm feared him.

sentences.zh: 餘疑愛變，謀奪其權。

translations.literal: Yu suspected Ai would change and plotted to seize his power.
translations.idiomatic: Yu suspected Ai's treachery and plotted to seize his power.

sentences.zh: 愛因餘祭廟，夜殺餘。

translations.literal: Ai because Yu sacrificed at the temple killed Yu at night.
translations.idiomatic: Ai killed Yu on a night of ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 文成葬以王禮，諡曰隱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng buried him with princely rites, posthumous name Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng buried him with princely rites, posthumous name Yin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：梟獍為物，天實生之。

translations.literal: Discussion says: The owl and jackal as creatures—heaven truly bore them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Owls and jackals are creatures heaven itself begets.

sentences.zh: 觀夫元紹所懷，蓋亦特鐘沴氣。

translations.literal: Observing what Yuan Shao harbored, he also especially received perverse qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's heart, they say, was specially steeped in foul breath.

sentences.zh: 平陽以降，並多夭促；

translations.literal: From Pingyang down, all many early deaths;
translations.idiomatic: From Pingyang downward, princes died young;

sentences.zh: 英才武略，未顯高年。

translations.literal: talent and martial stratagem did not show in advanced years.
translations.idiomatic: talent and arms rarely reached old age.

sentences.zh: 靖、簡二王，為時稱首。

translations.literal: Princes Jing and Jian, for the time were called foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Jing and Jian were the age's foremost.

sentences.zh: 鑒既有聲，渾亦見器。

translations.literal: Jian already had reputation; Hun also was regarded as vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Jian won renown; Hun was esteemed as well.

sentences.zh: 霄、繼荷遇太和之日，名位豈妄及哉！

translations.literal: Xiao and Ji bore favor in Taihe's days—name and rank, could they be reached in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao and Ji flourished under Taihe—who could match their rank lightly?

sentences.zh: 叉階緣寵私，遂亂天下，殺身全祀，固為幸焉。

translations.literal: Cha climbed by favor and private ties, then disordered the realm; killing the body yet preserving sacrifice—indeed fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Cha rose by favor and wrecked the realm; to die yet keep his rites was fortune enough.

sentences.zh: 樂平、樂安俱以將領自效，竟以憂迫而逝，驗克終之為鮮。

translations.literal: Princes of Leping and Le'an both by general's merit served effect; in the end because of anxious pressure they passed—proof that completing the end is rare.
translations.idiomatic: Leping and Le'an served as generals yet died under strain—few finish the course.

sentences.zh: 莊王才力智謀，一時之傑，與夫建寧、新興，不同日也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang's talent, strength, wisdom, and stratagem—a hero of the time; with Princes of Jianning and Xinxing, not the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang's wit was a hero of his day, unlike Jianning and Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 太武之子，秦、晉才賢。

translations.literal: Among Taiwu's sons, Qin and Jin were talented.
translations.idiomatic: Among Taiwu's sons, Qin and Jin showed talent.

sentences.zh: 而翰之遇酷，倚伏豈可量矣。

translations.literal: Yet Han's meeting with cruelty—how can fortune and misfortune be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Han met cruelty—who can measure fortune's turn?

sentences.zh: 臨淮之後，彧為盛德；

translations.literal: After Huaiyang, Yu was abundant virtue;
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiyang, Yu bore abundant virtue;

sentences.zh: 廣陽之世，嘉實為美，深之闕惡於元徽，所謂盜憎之義。

translations.literal: In Guangyang's generation Jia was truly beautiful; Shen's faults toward Yuan Hui—the so-called thief hates righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang's Jia was fair; Shen's evil toward Yuan Hui was the thief hating the just.

sentences.zh: 作之見殺，不基晚歟！

translations.literal: Zuo being seen killed—not a late foundation!
translations.idiomatic: That Zuo was slain was no late ruin!
